\subsection{Manuscript 08: Names to Numbers}\label{cdc:sec:ms08}
\srcnote{\wtag{} Manuscripts 08--11 were delivered in batch~62 of ProveIt's incoming reports, after the rest of this report had been written; each is printed in a Part of its own (Parts~X--XIII), and this section gives its title page, abstract, status statement and introduction. Title-page heading ``Computability / Diophantine representation''; subtitle ``Exact Quartic Certificates for Dynamic Heaps and Local Graph Computation''. ``A research article developed for the ProveIt program'', 30 September 2026; pinned at \texttt{4e128356d}. Batch~62, manuscript~01 (\path{Names_to_Numbers_Diophantine_Heaps.zip}). Printed here (abstract, status, Section~1) and in Part~X (Sections 2--14 and both appendices).}

% ---- manuscript 08, lines 72-96 ----
\paragraph{Abstract.}
An effective finite-trace computational model already has a Diophantine
halting relation by MRDP. The more discriminating problem is to preserve the internal structure of
its computations: memory reads must see the latest write, fresh object names
must not create spurious multiplicity, and arithmetic helper variables must
not introduce extra witnesses. We construct an exact compiler for these
requirements over the nonnegative integers.

For a log padded to $N$ memory events and any sorting network with $C$
comparators, the memory layer uses exactly $10C+4N-3$ auxiliary variables and
$10C+7N-4$ quadratic residual equations. Their sum of squares is one polynomial
of degree at most four. A fixed log has exactly one natural auxiliary solution
when it is valid and none otherwise. Addresses and stored values need not be
bounded in advance. An implemented bitonic network gives
$C=N k(k+1)/4$ for $N=2^k$; substituting an established linearithmic sorting
network gives an $O(N\log N)$ existence result.

A second construction canonically numbers objects by their ordered birth
events. For fixed local heap programs this yields a bijection between natural
zeros and finite runs modulo fresh-name permutations, while retaining genuine
schedule choices. We give a direct Turing-machine simulation by pointer-only
two-stack heaps, a transfer theorem for bounded-local graph programs, a
canonical quadratic treatment of inactive branches, explicit height bounds,
and a computability obstruction to existential certification of perpetual
memory safety. The archive contains the implemented memory compiler,
executable checks, and a numerical certificate.

\textbf{Status and scope.} Full mathematical proofs are supplied for the stated
constructions. The memory layer and pointer-log demonstrations are implemented
and tested; the complete source-language compiler is a mathematical
construction, not a delivered implementation. This work is not Lean-certified
or independently refereed. The specific assembly and quantitative contracts
are research contributions of this draft; historical priority is not
established. No resolution of the general finite-fold or single-fold MRDP
questions is claimed.
\end{resultbox}

\subsubsection{The problem being solved}
\paragraph{Beyond the existence of a representing polynomial}
Suppose a computational system has effectively encoded finite configurations
and an effectively checkable one-step relation. Finite accepting computations
can be enumerated. Consequently, the existence of some polynomial representing
acceptance is already a consequence of MRDP. Merely replacing a Turing machine
by an unusual substrate does not, by itself, produce a new representability
theorem. The repository's formal MRDP development already provides this
existence-level foundation \cite{repo-h10}.

The useful additional questions concern the representation itself. Can it
recognize arbitrary dynamic memory accesses without writing a complete heap
at every time? Can it preserve the number of computational witnesses? Can it
remove the infinitely many choices of otherwise irrelevant fresh names?
Can all the resulting equations remain quadratic, so that one sum of squares
has degree at most four? Finally, which parts survive when the time bound is
removed?

We answer these questions for a precisely specified class of finite
computations. The central achievement is a \emph{composable exact certificate
contract}, rather than a claim that a previously non-Diophantine universal
substrate has become Diophantine.

\paragraph{Main results at a glance}
Throughout, $\N=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$. An auxiliary solution always means a solution
in $\N$, not an unrestricted integer or real solution.

\begin{theorem}[Overview]\label{cdc:nh:thm:overview}
The following constructions are effective.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2em]
\item A length-$m\ge1$ memory log can be represented by one nonnegative
quartic polynomial with unique auxiliary extension for every valid source log.
For $N=2^{\lceil\log_2m\rceil}$ and a $C$-comparator sorting network, the exact
memory-layer counts are
\[
 A_{\rm mem}=10C+4N-3,\qquad E_{\rm mem}=10C+7N-4.
\]
Here the $3m$ address/flag/value source coordinates are not included in
$A_{\rm mem}$, and $E_{\rm mem}$ counts emitted residual slots, including
constant-zero slots from padding.
\item For a fixed finite bounded-local heap program, an initial heap of $S$
objects, and a bound of $T$ macrosteps, accepting runs modulo fresh-name
permutations have a bijective quartic representation with
$O((S+T)\log^2(S+T+2))$ variables under the implemented bitonic construction.
An established $O(N\log N)$ sorting network improves the mathematical bound
to $O((S+T)\log(S+T+2))$.
\item A pointer-only two-stack substrate is Turing complete and satisfies the
local hypotheses of (ii). Its source semantics requires no arithmetic on
object names.
\item Finite memory faults in this class admit Diophantine representations,
but the parameterized property that a deterministic program is memory-safe
forever need not admit any existential polynomial representation.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

The separate theorems below establish all four assertions. The constants in
(ii) depend on the fixed program, its record width, its maximum number of
accesses and births per macrostep, and the chosen local instruction
certificates. The result does not assert one small constant for arbitrary
source languages or arbitrary program descriptions.

\paragraph{What is, and is not, quotiented}
The quotient in (ii) removes names of dynamically born objects. It does
\emph{not} identify two different rewrite schedules, two different chosen
redex occurrences, or two derivations merely because their final graphs are
isomorphic. The initial objects have fixed identities, and objects born in a
single macrostep occupy specified ordered output slots. These qualifications
are essential to the bijection, not presentation details.

For a deterministic source program with a fixed input and a fixed padding
convention, at most one run survives. For a nondeterministic source program,
there can be many zeros, but exactly one for each retained computational run.
This is bounded, witness-faithful compilation. It is not a fixed-arity
single-fold representation of an arbitrary recursively enumerable set.

\paragraph{Abstract.}
The existence of Diophantine representations of computable physical or
combinatorial systems is an immediate consequence of the
Matiyasevich--Robinson--Davis--Putnam theorem once a finite execution can be
recognized. That observation alone says little about the degree of an
explicit certificate, its size, or the meaning and multiplicity of its
witnesses. This article addresses these issues through two complementary
results.

First, for every finite number of input coordinates, the sets represented
by an integer polynomial of degree at most three that is nonnegative on
the whole real nonnegative orthant are exactly the semilinear sets.
Every semilinear set already has such a representation of degree two,
and can in fact be represented with exactly one natural witness per member.
Degree four, in contrast, represents every computably enumerable set.
The lower bound follows from a facewise rigidity lemma: the zeros of a
nonnegative cubic in an open convex region form an affine slice determined
by a Hessian kernel. The natural zero set is consequently a finite union
of natural solutions of rational affine systems. We give both an elementary
existence proof and an effective version using real-algebraic sampling.
Even the set of squares requires degree four within this positivity class.

Second, finite producibility in the seeded abstract Tile Assembly Model
admits a direct, order-free, assembly-faithful compiler. Each occupied site
carries its unique first-arrival round. Two local threshold tests, one at
the preceding round and one a round earlier, characterize these ranks
without a time-expanded tableau. Boolean labels, comparisons, and local
conjunctions are enforced by affine equations with unique nonnegative
slacks. Summing their squares gives a convex quadratic with one natural
zero per producible labelled assembly. We give exact variable and equation
counts, a whole-grid terminality extension, an antimatroid interpretation,
and counterexamples explaining why negative interactions and static
partial-order schedules require separate treatment.

These results fit the two existing interfaces in ProveIt: its finite-witness
MRDP theorem and its Presburger decision procedure. The accompanying
implementation verifies four complete small assembly families, checks
rank uniqueness by exhaustive finite search, and exports literal affine
systems and witnesses. The combination distinguishes bounded spatial
certificates from fixed-arity universal equations and identifies a sharp
obstruction to compressing the latter into nonnegative cubics.

\noindent\textbf{Keywords.} Diophantine representation; semilinear set;
nonnegative cubic; MRDP; abstract Tile Assembly Model; canonical witness;
monotone activation; Presburger arithmetic.

\subsubsection{Questions, contributions, and the repository boundary}
\label{cdc:of:sec:introduction}

\paragraph{Two questions worth separating}
A computational substrate may be a register machine, a term-rewriting
system, a growing tile assembly, or any other effectively described
transition system. For finite reachability, MRDP gives an existential
polynomial after an encoding is chosen. A useful next question is not
merely whether a polynomial exists, but what arithmetic structure is
necessary and what its solutions actually count.

We study the following two questions.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{Q\arabic*.},leftmargin=2.7em]
\item Can an everywhere nonnegative cubic be a universal arithmetic
certificate, or is there an exact obstruction below degree four?
\item Can a genuinely asynchronous spatial computation be represented
without choosing a construction order, with exactly one witness for each
final labelled object and an explicit linear-size certificate?
\end{enumerate}
The first question is answered by the complete classification in
Theorem~\ref{cdc:of:thm:classification}. The second is answered for seeded
irreversible self-assembly by Theorem~\ref{cdc:of:thm:compiler}, including the
unique earliest-rank characterization in Theorem~\ref{cdc:of:thm:ranks}.
Neither question is treated by invoking universality alone.

The hypotheses of Q1 are deliberately precise: nonnegativity holds at
\emph{all real nonnegative assignments to inputs and witnesses jointly}.
For Q2 the finite candidate domain is compiler data, and the number of
arithmetic coordinates grows with that domain. This is not a fixed-arity
single-fold representation of an unbounded halting predicate.

\paragraph{What was inspected in ProveIt}
The repository was inspected at commit
\begin{center}\small\texttt{4e128356d0ef75308be8ed405d89aea2ffdb8a57}.\end{center}
The source file
\path{Computability/HilbertTenthProblem/Lean/Diophantine/MRDP.lean}
contains the finite-polynomial theorem \code{Diophantine.mrdp} and its
converse \code{mrdp_iff}. Its quantifiers choose one finite witness
number and one integer polynomial before the natural input is supplied.
The same source exposes \code{mrdp_dioph_iff} through Mathlib's
\code{Dioph} interface~\cite{repo-mrdp-lean}.

The Hilbert-tenth README and status register document the surrounding
Jones-paper formalizations, finite-trace infrastructure, and the
separate status of numerical universal certificates~\cite{repo-h10}.
No optimized operation count in that work is used as an assumption here.
In particular, this article does not claim to improve the repository's
75-operation certificate.

The directory \path{Logic/PresburgerArithmetic} documents an executable
Cooper quantifier-elimination development and the interface
\path{PresburgerArithmetic.Formula.presburgerArithmetic_decidable}
~\cite{repo-presburger}. The present classification therefore connects
two relevant repository themes: arithmetic relations that collapse to
Presburger arithmetic, and relations that require full MRDP strength.
These are source inspections, not a fresh build or an independent axiom
audit of the repository.

\paragraph{Prior work and the meaning of the contribution}
Semilinear sets and Presburger-definable sets coincide by the classical
work of Ginsburg and Spanier~\cite{ginsburg-spanier}. The geometry of
zeros of copositive quadratic forms already uses support faces and
positive-semidefinite principal submatrices~\cite{hildebrand}.
Ahmadi and Zhang study the geometry and computation of local minima of
cubics; their Lemma~4.2 and Theorem~4.3 give closely related
Hessian-kernel and line-restriction phenomena~\cite{ahmadi-zhang}.
Our short geometric argument is included in full; the arithmetic
classification is not presented as a discovery of those antecedents.

The seeded abstract Tile Assembly Model is an established model of
algorithmic self-assembly. Its computational and intrinsic universality
are documented in~\cite{doty-universal,alseth-patitz}. Producibility and
compatible unions also have a substantial literature. For example,
Doty's polynomial-time results in~\cite{doty-hierarchical} concern the
\emph{hierarchical} model, which is not the seeded single-tile model
compiled here. We do not conflate the two.

The contribution developed here is the combination of a precise
positivity-restricted degree classification and a completely specified,
order-free arithmetic compiler with exact witness semantics. All claimed
mathematical implications have proofs below. Establishing publication
priority for this formulation would require a broader literature and
expert review; no claim of historical priority or a named published open
problem's resolution is made.

\subsection{Manuscript 10: Sharp Pumping Bounds and Canonical Diophantine Certificates for Priority Arithmetic Computation}\label{cdc:sec:ms10}
\srcnote{\wtag{} Subtitle ``FRACTRAN, ordered multiset rewriting, and finitely certified nontermination''. An AI-assisted research manuscript (its author line, recorded in \cref{cdc:sec:provenance}, names only the assistant), 30 September 2026; pinned at \texttt{4e128356d}. Batch~62, manuscript~04 (\path{ProveIt_Priority_Pumping_Diophantine.zip}). Printed here (abstract, status, Section~1) and in Part~XII (Sections 2--14 and the three appendices).}

% ---- manuscript 10, lines 52-74 ----
\paragraph{Abstract.}
An ordered arithmetic program chooses the first enabled rule. This priority
condition is precisely what a naive product-of-transitions certificate loses.
We study finite repetitions of a prescribed instruction word, retaining all
priority tests. For rules consuming vectors bounded by $H$ coordinatewise,
we prove a sharp, word-length-independent pumping theorem: if some initial
state executes $2H+1$ copies of the word, then every finite number of copies
is executable from a suitable initial state. A closed formula computes the
exact repetition capacity, including the case of infinite capacity; a
three-fraction family attains capacity $2H$.

We also construct an explicit polynomial of degree at most four for the
endpoint relation of a fixed repeated word. The program coefficients,
initial state, repetition count, and final state are free natural-number
inputs. Every true instance has exactly one auxiliary solution. The number
of auxiliary variables is linear in the word length and the number of
priority comparisons, independent of the repetition count. The construction
uses totalized comparisons and Euclidean division rather than an appeal to
MRDP. Finally, we characterize infinite periodic instruction tails, prove
that existence of an eventually periodic instruction trace is computably
enumerable complete even for one fixed squarefree-denominator program, and
give a six-fraction nonperiodic computation with
a finite affine macro certificate. Complete proofs, a reproducible compiler,
explicit polynomial data, finite tests, and a formalization roadmap are included.

\subsubsection{The research problem and the repository boundary}
\label{cdc:pf:sec:context}

\paragraph{Why another Diophantine computation construction?}
The statement that a Turing-complete effective substrate has a Diophantine
halting relation is a consequence of MRDP, not a new representation theorem
by itself. A useful additional result should preserve information that this
existence statement does not quantify: priority, witness multiplicity,
certificate size, endpoints, or a specific compression mechanism.

The relevant ProveIt development already supplies MRDP in both directions
and a substantial formalization of Jones's constructions
\cite{repo-h10}. Its research note on alternative arithmetic machines
identifies the first-applicable-rule requirement as an obstacle to a shorter
FRACTRAN history compiler \cite{repo-variants}. The vendored Rocq/Coq
library also contains Diophantine one-step, transitive-closure, stopping, and
evaluation relations for FRACTRAN \cite{repo-coq}. Thus a bare translation of
FRACTRAN halting would duplicate existing work.
\wtag{} Part~VII of this report prints another bounded FRACTRAN certificate with first-applicable-fraction priority, on raw integers (\cref{cdc:wf:thm:fractran}).

We instead ask three narrower, quantitative questions.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Can an arbitrarily long repetition of a prescribed word be checked
without enumerating its individual steps, while preserving every priority test?
\item Is there a sharp upper bound on a word's finite repetition capacity
when the initial state is allowed to vary?
\item Can the accelerated checker be made into a small, explicit polynomial
with a unique auxiliary witness, rather than merely an existential arithmetic formula?
\end{enumerate}
The answers are affirmative. A secondary question---how much nontermination
can be captured by finite descriptions---exposes both a useful extension and
an unavoidable incompleteness boundary.

\paragraph{Main conclusions}
For an ordered program with production and consumption matrices
$A,B\in\N^{m\times d}$, let
\[
 H=\max_{i,p} B_{ip}.
\]
For any fixed nonempty instruction word $w$, the exact capacity
$\Capacity(w)$ belongs to $\{0,1,\ldots,2H\}\cup\{\infty\}$.
Theorem~\ref{cdc:pf:thm:capacity} gives a closed formula, and
Theorem~\ref{cdc:pf:thm:sharp} proves that $2H$ cannot be reduced.
The statement is about existence of a seed for each finite repetition
count; it is not automatically about one seed supporting an infinite run.

For $w=(j_0,\ldots,j_{\ell-1})$, with one-based instruction indices, put
\begin{equation}\label{cdc:pf:eq:RS}
 R=\sum_{r=0}^{\ell-1}j_r,\qquad S=dR.
\end{equation}
The endpoint compiler in Theorem~\ref{cdc:pf:thm:quartic} has
\begin{align}
 n_z&=29S+3d\ell+12d+3R+3\ell,\label{cdc:pf:eq:nz-intro}\\
 n_f&=32S+3d\ell+15d+4R+4\ell+1\label{cdc:pf:eq:nf-intro}
\end{align}
auxiliary variables and quadratic residual equations, respectively. Their
sum of squares is the promised quartic polynomial. These are counts for the
specified unoptimized compiler, not minimality claims.

Theorem~\ref{cdc:pf:thm:infinite} characterizes infinite repetition by nonnegative
drift and a permanent zero-drift blocker for every earlier rule. Theorem~\ref{cdc:pf:thm:ep}
then shows that discovering an eventually periodic instruction tail is
computably enumerable complete, despite decidability of checking a supplied
tail. Section~\ref{cdc:pf:sec:nonperiodic} gives an explicit nonperiodic computation
that is nevertheless certified by a finite affine family of accelerated blocks.

\paragraph{Provenance and related work}
The repository inspection is pinned to commit
\begin{center}\small\texttt{4e128356d0ef75308be8ed405d89aea2ffdb8a57}.\end{center}
The inspected scope consists of the Hilbert-tenth-problem README, the
FRACTRAN alternatives note, and the vendored FRACTRAN Diophantine file.
This is not a repository-wide correctness audit or a build of its formal
libraries. The distinction matters because the historical alternatives note
uses a 90-operation baseline, while the newer README reports a 75-operation
complete certificate. Our residual counts measure a different object.

Conway's FRACTRAN uses the first fraction that produces an integer and
supports universal arithmetic computation \cite{conway1987}.
Larchey-Wendling and Forster use it as an intermediate model in a formal
proof of DPRM \cite{lf2022}. Acceleration of prescribed counter-machine paths
and flat schemas is well established; Barrett, Demri, and Deters discuss
Presburger descriptions of such runs \cite{bdd}, while Decker and Pirogov
study compressed path schemas for temporal verification \cite{dp}.
Our elementary interval analysis belongs to that tradition. We do not claim
that fixed-loop acceleration or quarticization by arithmetic circuits is new
in general. The specific package here is the exact first-applicable-rule
capacity calculation, its sharp bound, and a fully specified canonical
arithmetic compiler with an audited count.
\wtag{} Within this report: for a fixed program, single-fold quartic acceleration of the block relation is an instance of \cref{cdc:pt:thm:acceleration} (Part~IV), and the priority-free power of a fixed word is \cref{cdc:ct:prop:word-power} (Part~III). The new content of Part~XII is uniformity in the program entries, the priority capacity formula and the sharp threshold $2H+1$.

Manuscript~11 has no separate status statement; its scope statements are the last two paragraphs of its Section~1, printed below.}

% ---- manuscript 11, lines 59-79 ----
\paragraph{Abstract.}
We give an explicit compiler from deterministic increment/decrement register
machines to priority reaction systems in which every reaction consumes exactly
two molecules and produces exactly two, and only one reaction has low priority.
An eight-register universal source machine yields a fixed system with 61 species
and 62 reactions. Its closed finite-reservoir instances are finite-state;
universality holds after existentially quantifying the initial reservoir, or
in the corresponding open-reservoir semantics. The least sufficient reservoir
is exactly the peak total source-register population minus its initial value.

We construct ordinary quartic polynomial certificates whose natural solutions
are in bijection with bounded, canonically padded computations. For a fixed
resource cutoff, these certificates are single-fold and have explicit size and
height bounds. The minimum-reservoir relation is primitive recursive and even
decidable in logarithmic space on unary inputs. Nevertheless, a finite-fold
Diophantine representation of this one relation is equivalent to the general
finite-fold conjecture; the analogous single-fold equivalence also holds.
We additionally prove a priority-erasure obstruction using a self-contained
coverability argument, extend the canonicalization principle to Pareto-minimal
resources, and provide a tested compiler and an expanded example polynomial.
The results are normal-form constructions and reductions, not a resolution of
the finite-fold conjecture or a claim of record-small universality.

% ---- manuscript 11, lines 87-168 ----
\subsubsection{Research question, contribution, and provenance}

\paragraph{Why another computational substrate is not enough}
The MRDP theorem identifies computably enumerable relations with Diophantine
relations. Consequently, proving that a new finitely described computational
substrate has Diophantine halting sets is often an immediate corollary of an
already established universality theorem. A useful contribution should retain
something that this abstract existence argument forgets: resource usage,
operational semantics, an explicit low-degree certificate, or control of
arithmetic witness multiplicity.

ProveIt's Hilbert-tenth-problem development already provides the appropriate
existence machinery. Its MRDP guide distinguishes a fixed finite polynomial
representation from an explicit numerical degree bound or a practical
polynomial-generating algorithm. Its trace interface supplies bounded universal
quantification, exact iteration, and existential finite reachability
\cite{repo-mrdp,repo-trace}. These are the interfaces on which the present
work builds conceptually; our reaction construction and bounded polynomial
compiler do not assume any unproved repository theorem.

There is substantial existing work on register-machine arithmetization,
including Jones and Matiyasevich's exponential-Diophantine construction, and on
certified reductions through FRACTRAN \cite{jm1984,lf2022}.
Priority semantics and universal multiset rewriting are likewise established
subjects \cite{best-koutny,alhazov-verlan}. The objective here is not to rename
one of those models, but to prove a particular conjunction of restrictions
and exact correspondences.

\paragraph{What is proved here}
The principal structural result is an effective compiler with all of the
following properties simultaneously: two-to-two reactions, total molecule
conservation, a single shared low-priority fallback, determinism on legal
initial markings, and an exact resource threshold. For the universal instance,
the bound is 61 species and 62 reactions. These numbers are construction
bounds, not optimality claims.

The arithmetic result has two levels. At a fixed horizon we give the actual
quadratic residuals whose sum of squares is a quartic polynomial, and prove
uniqueness of every auxiliary variable. At a fixed resource cutoff we combine
two such traces to certify the \emph{least} sufficient resource. Finally, we
prove that compressing this particular decidable minimum-resource relation
into a fixed finite-fold polynomial would settle the general finite-fold
conjecture. This locates a genuine unresolved issue rather than silently
assuming it away.

The research questions answered affirmatively are construction questions
formulated in this manuscript. We do not assert that their exact formulations
were previously published open problems. The contribution is the explicit
compiler, its exact quantitative and witness-preserving analysis, and the
resulting normal form. Historical priority for this combination has not been
established by an exhaustive literature review.

\paragraph{Three semantic qualifications}
A finite closed reservoir cannot provide an infinite supply of memory. Every
closed instance below is finite-state, and its acceptance is decidable.
The undecidable question is whether \emph{some} finite initial reservoir
suffices. The open-reservoir interpretation is the genuinely Turing-complete
single-machine semantics. These two statements must not be conflated.

The word \emph{fuel} means reusable storage reserve: a decrement returns a
molecule to the reservoir. It is not a monotonically expended energy budget.
The exact formula therefore measures peak register population, not running
time.

Finally, priority is an ideal execution rule, not an assertion about physical
reaction rates. Section~\ref{cdc:rx:sec:physical} proves that merely assigning a large
but finite rate to the high-priority reaction does not implement the exact
zero test used here.

\paragraph{Source and verification scope}
The repository review was targeted to the Hilbert-tenth-problem README, the
MRDP guide, and the trace implementation. The trace source was read at revision
\path{4e128356d0ef75308be8ed405d89aea2ffdb8a57}. \wtag{} [The manuscript adds that a later read of the
live branch returned \path{ccfb084adaa2f32e8d2738a25f82a00377fb3a8c}; the files it cites are identical at the two commits.] No assertion is made
that every newly incoming report was reviewed. The paper cites the inspected
interfaces, not a purported exhaustive novelty audit of the repository.

All new mathematical statements below are proved in ordinary mathematics.
The supplied Python tests were executed, but the new construction has not been
Lean-formalized or independently refereed. The inherited universality of the
source machine is a literature dependency, not something established by finite
simulation tests.

\paragraph{Abstract.}
A generic application of the Matiyasevich--Robinson--Davis--Putnam theorem
represents a computably enumerable execution property by a polynomial, but
does not expose its operational meaning or control auxiliary multiplicity.
We develop a different route for finite particle-routing networks: replace the
entire execution history by prefix counts and a canonical last-exit forest.

For a fixed routing topology with $n$ active vertices, $s$ absorbing sinks,
and $m$ run-length blocks, we construct one integer polynomial of total degree
at most four with exactly $4n+4m+s$ natural witness coordinates. Initial chip
counts and all run lengths are parameters. Its natural zero set above each
parameter tuple is empty for nontermination and a singleton for termination;
the unique root includes the exact firing counts and every sink output.
The construction uses $6n+2m+s$ residual equations of degree at most two.
A second compiler handles periods represented by shared concatenation
grammars, with size linear in the grammar at the level of variables and
residual equations.

The representation of the routing instructions matters. Circuit-defined
periods already encode Boolean counting in a one-vertex acyclic network.
More sharply, an explicitly constructed one-router system has a uniformly
polynomial-time prefix-rank function and an eventually constant stack on
every input, yet has computably enumerable complete halting behavior. Its
single possible sink event occurs at firing $2^T$, where $T$ is a universal
machine's first halting time. We prove that giving this one monotone,
polynomial-time rank function a single-fold, respectively finite-fold,
Diophantine graph is equivalent to the corresponding representation
principle for all computably enumerable sets.

The last-exit mechanism is classical. The contributions developed here are
explicit canonical algebraic compilers, their quantitative accounting, and
precise representation-boundary theorems. All proofs are supplied; executable
exact-arithmetic checks and a sparse polynomial compiler accompany the paper.
Priority for these refinements has not been established, and the new
results have not been formalized in Lean.

% ---- manuscript 12, lines 116-202 ----
\subsubsection{The research problem and the claims made here}\label{cdc:rt:sec:intro}

\paragraph{Beyond a black-box application of MRDP}
The ProveIt repository provides a natural foundation for studying arithmetic
representations of computation. Its Hilbert's tenth problem development exposes
\code{Diophantine.mrdp} and its converse: a computably enumerable subset of
$\N$ is the projection of the natural zero set of a fixed integer polynomial.
The repository's interface allows input zero and natural witnesses, and does
not claim that the auxiliary witnesses are unique or provide a practical
polynomial-generating algorithm \cite{repo-h10,repo-mrdp}.

\wtag{} [ProveIt does formalize the single-fold \emph{exponential} representation of every enumerable set (\cref{cdc:bd:rem:sfu}); the missing uniqueness concerns ordinary polynomials. The files cited here are unchanged between the pin \texttt{e18718e83} and this write.]

Thus ``this effective substrate has Diophantine halting'' is usually not the
interesting conclusion. The useful questions are more structural. Can an
arithmetic certificate retain the exact output and firing counts? Can it avoid
one row per computation step? Can every auxiliary choice be made canonical?
Can instructions be compressed without expanding their repeated actions?
Finally, which of these benefits survive when the underlying model becomes
Turing complete?

Here a \emph{single-fold representation} of a relation $A(\mathbf x)$ means a
polynomial $Q(\mathbf x,\mathbf w)$ such that
\[
 A(\mathbf x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists\mathbf w\in\N^r\;Q(\mathbf x,\mathbf w)=0,
\]
with at most one complete tuple $\mathbf w$ for each $\mathbf x$.
A \emph{finite-fold representation} requires only finitely many witness tuples.
The adjective applies to \emph{all} auxiliary coordinates, not merely to a
unique decoded computation hidden inside a highly nonunique arithmetic
encoding. Parameters and witnesses must also be kept distinct: fixed
polynomial arity is a stronger requirement than one polynomial for each
externally chosen time bound.

\paragraph{Relation to previous work}
The conceptual starting point is established mathematics, not a claim of a
new least-action principle. Friedrich and Levine characterize abelian-stack
aggregation by a local balance condition and an acyclic final rotor structure,
and use that characterization to compute final states without traversing all
intermediate states \cite{friedrich-levine}. Bond and Levine develop the general abelian
network framework \cite{bond-levine}. For the one-token switching problem ARRIVAL,
G\"artner and coauthors give unique verifiable run-profile certificates and
prove membership in $\UP\cap\coUP$ \cite{arrival}. Fearnley and coauthors
explicitly study switching periods encoded by binary run lengths and extend
structural certificate methods to succinct switching games \cite{switching}.
In particular, neither run-length compression nor the use of last exits is
new here.

The paper specializes and recompiles these mechanisms in a way suited to
Diophantine research. We use zero-retention routing to absorbing sinks, permit
arbitrarily many input chips, make every slack and forest-height variable
unique, count the exact coordinates, and keep the run lengths themselves as
polynomial parameters. We also give a grammar-DAG compiler and explicit
counterexamples to overly broad generalizations. All arguments for this model
are proved below, rather than imported by analogy from a slightly different
aggregation convention.

\paragraph{A contribution and limitation ledger}
The central positive result is Theorem~\ref{cdc:rt:thm:rle}: the parametric quartic
with $4n+4m+s$ natural witness coordinates. Its grammar counterpart is
Theorem~\ref{cdc:rt:thm:grammar}. The resulting certificates have polynomial binary
length on finite succinct instances, and a trap-collapse construction supplies
canonical certificates for both outcomes of the termination question
(Theorem~\ref{cdc:rt:thm:classify}).

The central boundary result is Theorem~\ref{cdc:rt:thm:universal}: one uniform,
polynomial-time rank routine defines eventually constant stacks with universal
halting behavior. Theorem~\ref{cdc:rt:thm:bottleneck} then identifies the exact
single-fold and finite-fold obstruction for that routine, with an explicit
$2r+3$ witness bound conditional on a local $r$-witness representation.
These are positive mathematical constructions and reductions, not claims
that the unrestricted representation principles have been proved.

No claimed result here gives a polynomial-time algorithm for finding the
unique routing certificate. No claimed result improves a universal
variable--degree record. The polynomial families for finite compressed
networks have dimensions depending on the network description. The
one-router universal construction uses an unbounded counter and a fixed
bounded-simulation algorithm; it is not a finite-state rotor in disguise.
We distinguish these points because confusing them would turn useful
structural results into false breakthrough claims.

The bibliography establishes relevant prior art but is not a complete
priority search for every formulation below. The explicit refinements are
presented as research results developed and proved in this article, with
priority unverified. The accompanying Python checks are independent finite
sanity checks, not substitutes for the proofs or a Lean kernel audit.

\paragraph{Abstract.}
% ---- manuscript 13, lines 70-97 ----
A small controller does not make graph memory free. Motivated by an explicit
wiring obstruction in the ProveIt repository, we study precisely how much
port incidence a sound arithmetic representation must preserve, and how to
preserve it without storing the entire graph at every time step.

The first main result is a sharp separation theorem. If $M\ne N$ are perfect
matchings of $2n$ labelled ports and $Q$ is a uniformly random matching, then
closing $M$ and $N$ with $Q$ gives different cyclic-wire parities with
probability between $2/5$ and $2/3$. Both constants are optimal, and the
equality cases are classified. An explicit recurrence proves this for every
$n$. Consequently, even one-bit contextual observations force lossless
wiring summaries; conversely, $O(n\log n)$ nonadaptive one-bit probes suffice
for simultaneous identification of all matchings.

The second main result is a constructive bounded-horizon compiler. An
interaction-combinator history with $C_0$ initial cells, $F$ free ports and
$T$ sequential interactions has a natural-number Diophantine certificate
with $O(C_0+F+T)$ variables and quadratic equations, or one polynomial of
degree at most four. Exact cyclic-wire counts are preserved. The construction
uses constant-time port splicing and an exact, collision-free, large-integer
memory argument. For a fixed legal schedule, its ancillary witnesses can be
made unique. An executable sparse-polynomial generator implements the memory
component, and separate finite tests check the combinatorial and rewriting
lemmas.

These are proved results within the stated models, not a claim to a new
smallest universal polynomial or to a general single-fold MRDP theorem.
Historical priority for the sharp separation theorem has not been certified.

\small

receipts, and an expanded example quartic. No Lean
build or independent peer review is claimed.

\subsubsection{Research target, scope, and relation to existing work}
\label{cdc:ew:sec:scope}

\paragraph{A specific unresolved repository interface}

The ProveIt note \emph{A finite wiring obstruction for interaction
combinators} exhibits two four-cell nets with identical labelled underlying
graph, agent counts, port-type histogram and initially active pair, but
different agent-free reachability. It explicitly leaves a topology-aware
arithmetic compiler open \cite{repo-icobs}. This is a useful target:
it is not enough merely to invoke the fact that every computably enumerable
relation is Diophantine. One wants to know what the graph memory must retain,
how local rewiring is certified, and which costs grow with the computation.

We address two precise questions.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{Contextual information question.} Can an encoding forget part of a
matching while remaining exact under every possible wiring context, even if
the observable is only cyclic-wire parity?

\textbf{Bounded compilation question.} Can exact interaction-combinator
histories, including cyclic components, be compiled with only linearly many
arithmetic coordinates, rather than a graph-sized tableau at every step?
\end{quote}

The answers are respectively \emph{no}, with a sharp probabilistic
strengthening, and \emph{yes}, with a completely specified arithmetic
construction. The first result is independent of the universality of the
substrate. The second applies to all six rules, not only the terminating
all-$\delta$ fragment used by the repository counterexample.

\paragraph{What is old, what is proved here, and what remains to be built}

Lafont's interaction combinators form a three-symbol, six-rule universal
interaction system \cite{lafont}. Port numbering is semantic, and isolated
cyclic wires belong to the formalism. Exact permutation-based gluing,
execution formulas and their associativity already occur in de Falco's
framework \cite{defalco}. Matching composition with a recorded loop scalar
also belongs to the established Brauer-category framework
\cite{lehrer-zhang}. None of those concepts is claimed as an invention here.

Memory verification by comparing suitable collections of access records has
a substantial prior history \cite{begkn,naor-parter-yogev}. Our arithmetic
variant uses a deterministically computed large integer in place of a random
field fingerprint, and proves the resulting natural-number zero set exactly.
The price is large witness height; this is not a cryptographic improvement.

The report's principal mathematical contribution is the explicit signed
closure recurrence and the sharp $2/5$--$2/3$ theorem, including its equality
cases. Its principal compilation contribution is the combination of exact
loop-preserving local rewriting, canonical sorted-memory witnesses, bounded
allocation, and a linear-description quartic family. These are new
derivations supplied for the project. A literature search located the
related frameworks above, but did not establish priority for these exact
statements; the report therefore makes no categorical claim that they have
never appeared elsewhere.

The attached code implements every interaction rule and both gluing
algorithms. It also implements the complete sparse-polynomial memory
component. The \emph{entire} interaction-net polynomial family is specified
and proved constructively in Sections~\ref{cdc:ew:sec:quadratic}--\ref{cdc:ew:sec:compiler},
but a fully instrumented exporter for every controller microstep is not
included. That implementation distinction does not replace, or enlarge, the
mathematical theorem.

\paragraph{Conventions and the size model}

Throughout, $\N=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$. Every quantified arithmetic coordinate is
natural; every polynomial has integer coefficients. A certificate with
$R$ quadratic residuals $E_1,\ldots,E_R$ can be replaced by
\begin{equation}\label{cdc:ew:eq:sos}
 P=\sum_{i=1}^{R}E_i^2.
\end{equation}
Over $\N$, $P=0$ is equivalent to all $E_i=0$. Thus $\deg P\le4$.
Degree four by itself is a standard normal-form phenomenon, not the novel
content of the compiler.

An \emph{external horizon} $T$ indexes a different finite polynomial for each
$T$. It is not an extra existential variable inside a single fixed-arity
polynomial. Linear size below means linearly many variables, residuals and
bounded-fanin arithmetic instructions in this family. It does not mean
linear bit complexity, nor a universal bound independent of $T$.

For contextual results, ports are labelled and there are no agents. For the
compiler, cells have canonical allocated identifiers and an explicitly
ordered interface. Exact equality of outputs refers to that labelling; an
arbitrary quotient by graph isomorphism is not silently included.

\paragraph{Abstract.}
% ---- manuscript 14, lines 94-114 ----
A recent ProveIt note exhibits two four-agent interaction nets with identical
coarse graph statistics but different agent-free reachability, and explicitly
leaves a topology-aware arithmetic compiler open. We address that bounded,
explicit-input interface rather than re-proving that a universal substrate
has some Diophantine representation. The central observation is that wire
suppression never traverses surviving agents: all temporary degree-two
vertices belong to the bounded rule interface. For binary annihilation this
interface has exactly ten partial-matching patterns. We give quadratic
formulas for the number of newly closed wires, quadratic extensions for the
surviving endpoint matching, and a sharp ten-state distinguishability result
for this local abstraction. A deterministic integer-product certificate then
checks an entire bounded random-access memory log with $17L-4$ auxiliary
coordinates and the same number of quadratic residuals. Its proof uses a
carry-free integer base, not a randomized fingerprint. Composing these
constructions yields an exact, loop-sensitive, witness-faithful quartic
family of size $O(C_0+f+T)$, with polynomial bit-length witnesses. A literal
36-access rewrite schedule, the soundness and uniqueness arguments, native
bounded-input loading, terminal predicates, implementation boundaries, and
research directions are included. Exhaustive and randomized checks compare
two independently organized reducers, including all 10,395 matchings on four
labelled binary cells.

\subsubsection{The research target and what is actually established}\label{cdc:nt:sec:intro}
\paragraph{A specific repository gap}
The motivating file is \emph{A finite wiring obstruction for interaction
combinators} in the ProveIt research continuation \cite{repo-icobs}.
It retains unusually substantial statistics---the labelled underlying graph,
port-type histogram, agent counts, and initially active pair---and nevertheless
finds two inputs that disagree on agent-free reachability. The note correctly
separates this obstruction from a lower bound on topology-aware certificates.
Its outstanding implementation interface is exact port memory, rewiring, and
cyclic-component accounting.

The surrounding repository already contains general witness-faithful memory
and bounded-local heap compilers \cite{repo-cdc}. Those results are a
foundation, not something to claim anew. The present continuation supplies a
small, exact interface for this particular graph semantics and proves its
composition with a self-contained capped-memory certificate. In particular,
we do not replace the graph by a count vector or treat wire topology as a
cost-free oracle.

The inspected repository snapshot is \texttt{6914ccca6685baf53b7a35f25efc89366c76ba74}. The obstruction note has Git blob
hash \texttt{764c982297342093307a0e831bc0d9ed5084c87f}. Repository findings here
refer to that snapshot, not to every incoming archive or every later commit.

\paragraph{Result ledger}
The central proved statements are as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Exact local topology.} A four-port annihilation is determined by
its partial internal matching and ordered external endpoints. A 23-residual
quadratic system has exactly one natural extension for each of the ten legal
internal patterns and none for any illegal pattern. Its output includes the
new cycle count. The local ten-state abstraction is minimal under a precisely
specified family of observations.
\item \textbf{An explicit memory bound.} For fixed positive $L,A,V$, validity
of a zero-initialized $L$-access log with address cap $A$ and value cap $V$ has
exactly one extension to a system of $17L-4$ quadratic equations in $17L-4$
auxiliaries. Its sum of squares is quartic. This bound includes all sorting,
range, and product witnesses.
\item \textbf{A complete bounded semantic interface.} A legal scheduled
interaction-combinator execution has exactly one natural zero of an
effectively constructed quartic family. There are $O(C_0+f+T)$ coordinates
and equations. Bare loops, self-wires between distinct ports of an agent,
parallel temporary edges, free ports, and fresh names are all covered.
\end{enumerate}
The last theorem is a mathematical construction, assembled from explicitly
described finite circuits and the memory system. The delivered code emits
the two arithmetic kernels and implements two reducers; it does not emit
the full unknown-schedule quartic. This distinction is maintained throughout.

\paragraph{Novelty and prior ingredients}
Lafont's interaction nets and universal interaction combinators are classical
\cite{lafont1990,lafont}. Precise permutation-based gluing, the execution
formula, and treatment of closed components are also established mathematics;
de Falco gives a particularly relevant account \cite{defalco}. Our contribution
is the explicit bounded Diophantine interface, its local resource ledger,
the particular capped-memory equations, and their proved composition.
The formulas are proved here, but independent priority for each elementary
lemma is not asserted. This is a resolution of a concrete repository-level
construction gap, not a claim that general arithmetization or interaction-net
semantics was previously unknown.

\subsection{Manuscript 15: No Ghost Wires}\label{cdc:sec:ms15}
\srcnote{\wtag{} Title-page heading ``Diophantine representations of computation''; subtitle ``Loop-Exact Quartic Certificates for Interaction Combinators'' and the line ``A topology-aware extension of the ProveIt research program''; ``Prepared for Vladimir Reshetnikov'', October 2, 2026; running head ``Research draft / October 2026''. Its PDF metadata, which names the AI provider, is recorded in \cref{cdc:sec:provenance}. Batch~78, manuscript~05 (\path{no_ghost_wires.zip}, inner directory \path{no_ghost_wires}; 25-page PDF). Printed here (abstract, status statement, Section~1) and in Part~XV (Sections 2--13 and Appendices A--C); its provenance note and claims ledger are shipped as \path{15-no-ghost-wires-PROVENANCE.md} and \path{15-no-ghost-wires-CLAIMS.md}.}

\paragraph{Abstract.}
% ---- manuscript 15, lines 74-97 ----
An interaction-combinator computation rewrites a port-labelled graph. Its wires
cannot be replaced by agent counts, edge counts, or port-type histograms: such
summaries can identify nets with different reachability behavior. Moreover,
rewriting may create closed wires with no remaining ports. We give an explicit
arithmetic treatment of both phenomena.

The central construction associates to the gluing of two matchings a permutation
whose boundary-containing orbits encode surviving wires and whose other orbits
encode closed components in pairs. A canonical minimum-and-distance certificate
for a permutation has exactly one natural witness: it uses $4n$ variables with
fixed successor indices, or $5n$ variables when the successor is selected by an
input permutation matrix. Its equations are quadratic. We combine this certificate
with literal templates for all six of Lafont's interaction-combinator rules,
obtaining a sum-of-squares polynomial of total degree at most four for each finite
lifetime schedule. For fixed endpoint nets, that polynomial has exactly one
natural zero if the scheduled computation is valid, and none otherwise.

We also prove a division-free matching-elimination identity, an order-independent
closed-loop accounting law, a sixteen-port locality bound, and a contextual
completeness result for boundary matchings together with loop counts. A complete
Python implementation exports the polynomial and its witness. Exact tests cover
46,234 permutations, 81,393 gluing instances, 412 contexts spanning all six rules,
and all 10,395 closed four-$\delta$ nets. The repository's distinguishing example
has a certificate with 126 witnesses and 169 quadratic residuals.

\begin{resultbox}
\small
% ---- manuscript 15, lines 101-105 ----
\textbf{Status.} Theorems are proved in this manuscript and supported by exact
finite checks. The work supplies the missing topology-aware compiler at finite
horizon. It does not supply a fixed-arity universal equation, establish historical
priority for the specific certificate, resolve finite-fold MRDP, or claim a new
Lean verification.
\end{resultbox}

% ---- manuscript 15, lines 111-181 ----
\subsubsection{The research question and the precise advance}

\paragraph{A concrete gap in the repository}
The ProveIt Hilbert's-tenth-problem project contains an extensive arithmetic
representation program, including an MRDP interface and research on alternative
computational substrates. The directly relevant starting point is its note
\emph{A finite wiring obstruction for interaction combinators}
\cite{repo-icobs}. That note constructs two four-agent nets with the same
labelled underlying graph, the same unordered port-type histogram, the same agent
types, and the same initially active pair. One reaches an agent-free net with two
cyclic wires; the other reaches a normal form containing two agents. Both
terminate. The distinction is reachability of the specified target, not
termination versus nontermination.

The note explicitly leaves a topology-aware arithmetic compiler to be supplied.
Its warning is justified: any representation whose entire dependence on the input
factors through the displayed summary must give the same answer for the two nets.
Changing the polynomial degree, increasing its number of witnesses, or appealing
to universality cannot repair information that has already been discarded.

We retain the exact port matching, implement every rule, and make cyclic wires
an explicit scalar component of the state. The advance is a concrete,
proof-backed finite-horizon compiler and a reusable arithmetic gluing theorem,
not a new assertion that this already-universal substrate is computable.

\paragraph{What is inherited and what is constructed here}
Interaction nets and the three-symbol, six-rule universal system are due to
Lafont \cite{lafont1990,lafont}. Matching composition with closed components
also belongs to the established diagrammatic setting of Brauer categories
\cite{lehrer-zhang}. Those facts are background, not novelty claims. In particular,
we do not rebrand ordinary matching concatenation as a newly discovered
mathematical operation.

The constructions developed here are the explicit canonical orbit certificate,
its low-degree selector form, the loop-exact integration with all six literal
rules, and the complete witness and residual ledger. The contextual and locality
lemmas explain exactly what can and cannot be compressed. Historical priority
for these particular arithmetic formulations has not been established.

permutation; no guessed component roots or unconstrained root slacks.\\

port-free cycles, including two-edge cycles.\\
All-six-rule compiler & Quadratic residuals and a quartic sum of squares for an

Multiplicity control & Exactly one witness per valid scheduled trace;
finite disjunction preserves one witness per successful schedule.\\

three gluing algorithms, and reproducible test receipts.\\

\end{center}

\paragraph{Conventions}
Throughout, $\N=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$. All polynomial coefficients are in $\Z$;
all parameters and existential witnesses range over $\N$. A \emph{quartic
certificate} means a polynomial of total degree at most four, usually displayed
as a sum of squares of quadratic residuals. Total degree counts endpoint
parameters as well as witnesses.

Agent identities and free-port labels are explicit. Auxiliary ports are ordered.
Statements about exact endpoints mean equality of these labelled data unless
an explicit renaming is supplied. A \emph{lifetime schedule} specifies the two
agent identities consumed at each step. Its legality with respect to agent
existence and types can be checked without knowing the wiring; whether the two
principal ports are actually connected is a separate arithmetic condition.

\paragraph{Abstract.}
% ---- manuscript 16, lines 63-92 ----
We construct an explicit integer polynomial of total degree at most three
whose unique natural-number zero certifies the stabilization of an arbitrary
nonnegative sandpile on a fixed finite undirected graph with a sink.
For $n$ nonsink vertices and $E$ undirected nonzero adjacencies,
the compact construction has $10n+6E$ certificate coordinates, including the
odometer, and $10n+7E$ manifestly nonnegative summands. A larger baseline
compiler and explicit inverse maps on their natural zero sets are also given.
The compact polynomial's arity is independent of the
number of legal topplings and of the magnitudes of the initial chip counts.
The construction replaces a computation history by a stable endpoint and the
canonical parallel burning ranks on the support of the proposed odometer.
A complementary-selector comparison gadget keeps the degree cubic while
forcing every auxiliary coordinate uniquely.

We extend the construction to finite boxes in an infinite periodic-plus-finite
sandpile. A one-layer exterior collar certifies that the finite computation is
also a global stabilization. An additional boundary condition chooses a unique
box radius. In this variable-arity family, all individual witnesses have
polynomial height in the radius and the maximum initial height. Combined with
Cairns's established three-dimensional universality theorem, this places the
unboundedness in spatial extent: there is no computable input-only bound on the
necessary radius. We also prove an explicit eventual affine-periodicity theorem
for finite-graph odometers, with exact minimal period determined by the rational
vector $L^{-1}h$.

The new object proposed here is the explicit canonical arithmetic compiler and
its spatial interface, not the classical burning method, sandpile universality,
or MRDP. The proofs are self-contained apart from the explicitly isolated
universality and MRDP dependencies. Literature priority is not established;
this manuscript and its code are not proof-assistant verified.

\subsubsection{The research target and the scope of the result}\label{cdc:sp:sec:scope}
A universal computational substrate is automatically a source of Diophantine
representations once its finite accepting computations are effectively
recognizable. That implication alone does not explain which parts of the
computation need to be represented. It also says nothing about the number of
witnesses, their multiplicity, the size of the equation, or the possibility of
checking a result without storing the entire execution.

The question pursued here is more specific:
\begin{quote}
Can one replace a potentially enormous sandpile toppling history by a sparse,
canonical, low-degree arithmetic certificate of its endpoint, and retain a
precise interface to a genuinely universal infinite sandpile?
\end{quote}
The answer developed below is affirmative for finite undirected sink graphs,
and for finite-support global stabilization on the nearest-neighbor lattice.
The certificate is cubic over natural witnesses. Its universality interface is
a family indexed by spatial radius, not a fixed cubic universal polynomial.

\paragraph{What was inspected in ProveIt}
The repository audit was pinned to revision
\begin{center}
\texttt{928ea97017a25ebe56d240c84f27d2275d818c75}.
\end{center}
The public MRDP guide specifies natural witnesses, integer polynomial
coefficients, and a fixed finite witness tuple before the free input is chosen
\cite{repo-mrdp}. This is an existence interface; the guide explicitly does not
supply a numerical complexity bound or a practical polynomial-generating
algorithm. We use that interface only in Section~\ref{cdc:sp:sec:mrdp}.

The Hilbert-tenth README at this revision reports separate 75-operation
certificate and 87-operation universal-polynomial constructions
\cite{repo-h10}. Those numbers belong to particular arithmetic ledgers.
They are not vertex counts, witness counts, or the number of summands in our
polynomial. No improvement to either repository bound is claimed here.

A nearby repository report already treats canonical routing certificates and
run-length-encoded switching systems. Its source ledger expressly distinguishes
those finite routing models from Cairns's infinite sandpiles
\cite{repo-rtsources}. The present construction uses a different invariant:
\emph{absence of a forbidden subconfiguration on the toppling support}, encoded
by canonical burning ranks. The audit is targeted rather than exhaustive; it
does not certify every existing repository result or establish worldwide
priority for the construction below.

\srcnote{\wtag{} Batch~78, 2 October 2026. The nearby report is this one: \path{12-rle-routing-SOURCES.md} is the source ledger of manuscript~12, whose text is Part~XIV. Manuscript~16 read that ledger, not this report's article, and so does not cite Part~XIV's question on infinite-background abelian computation, which it answers (see the note after that question), or the Part~IX theorems that its single-fold boundary instantiates (\cref{cdc:part:sandpile}).}

\paragraph{Established ingredients versus the present construction}
Dhar's burning method and the sandpile group are classical; J\'arai's survey
provides a precise account \cite{jarai}. Least-action validation of aggregate
odometer data also has precedents in fast simulation of abelian growth models
\cite{friedrich-levine}. We reprove the particular support criterion needed
here, instead of treating its arithmetic consequences as automatic.

Cairns proves undecidability of global halting for periodic-plus-finite
three-dimensional sandpiles by an effective Turing-machine simulation
\cite{cairns}. That simulation is an imported theorem, not a construction
implemented in the supplied code. The contribution proposed in this report is
the explicit low-degree certificate that can be attached to its finite
spatial restrictions.

Manuscript~16 names Dhar but cites J\'arai's survey for burning, and cites Friedrich--Levine for least-action validation; it claims neither mechanism.}

\paragraph{Abstract.}
% ---- manuscript 17, lines 87-118 ----
We construct canonical arithmetic certificates for computations whose scalar
observables have the form
\[
 f(n)=\sum_{b\in B}\sum_{k=0}^{d_b}c_{b,k}n^k b^n,
 \qquad c_{b,k}\in\Z,\quad B\subset\N_{>0},
 \qquad D=\sum_{b\in B}(d_b+1).
\]
The bases and degree bounds are fixed; the coefficients and the finite horizon
are inputs. A descending chain of operators $E-b$ annihilates the sequence.
Its levels have at most $2(D-j)-1$ maximal discrete sign intervals, and their
normalized values are monotone between the next level's boundaries. This yields
an exact local verifier with $D^2+1$ available interval slots and $O(D^3)$
quadratic arithmetic residuals, natural witnesses, and fixed-base power atoms.
There is exactly one complete witness tuple for every input, both on
$\{0,\ldots,T\}$ and on all of $\N$. The infinite verifier uses a coefficient
leading-sign test rather than a guessed asymptotic cutoff.

Consequences include canonical certificates for bounded and perpetual guard
satisfaction, first failure, and the least minimizer. We transfer the result to
integer affine updates with split rational spectrum, polynomial guards, and
triangular polynomial updates through finite-dimensional invariant monomial
spaces. Fixed schedules of repeated instruction words in a Turing-complete
register language can thus be certified without unrolling each repetition.

Two boundaries are proved. A rational rotation has linearly many sign runs,
so bounded raw sign diagrams cannot handle arbitrary spectra. More sharply,
an ordinary single-fold representation of the complete sign-chart graph of
$2^n-y$ is equivalent to the general single-fold conjecture; the analogous
finite-fold equivalence also holds. Order one needs no exponentiation at all.
An implemented parametric compiler exports complete quadratic residual lists,
power atoms, and expanded arithmetic quartics. Exact randomized, exhaustive
small-profile, parameter-uniformity, and mutation checks accompany the proofs.

% ---- manuscript 17, lines 126-219 ----
\subsubsection{From execution histories to sign geometry}\label{cdc:ps:sec:intro}
A usual arithmetic encoding of a computation introduces coordinates for its
successive states. If the computation takes $T$ steps, such a construction may
require a number of coordinates proportional to $T$. This is a perfectly valid
Diophantine representation, but it does not exploit a loop that executes the
same algebraic update an enormous number of times.

Suppose instead that a loop repeatedly applies $F$, and its legality at time
$n$ is determined by the signs of $g_1(F^n(x)),\ldots,g_q(F^n(x))$. When these
sequences are exponential polynomials with positive bases, they cannot have
arbitrarily complicated sign behavior. The relevant finite object is then not
a state tableau, but an exact sign diagram together with enough information
to verify that no intervening sign change was omitted.

The difficult part is the last phrase. Checking the endpoints of the whole
execution is unsound. For example,
\begin{equation}\label{cdc:ps:eq:example}
 f(n)=4^n-20\,2^n+64
\end{equation}
is positive at $0$ and $6$, but negative at $3$. Likewise, merely guessing all
zeros does not prove that another zero or an interval of negativity was not
missed. Our verifier resolves this through an annihilating difference chain.
A sign diagram at one level certifies monotonicity of a normalized sequence at
the preceding level, making endpoint tests sufficient there.

\subsubsection{What is already present in ProveIt}
The snapshot used here is \texttt{e58b724c25bd34533b7a5834cfcbe873dfa01288}. The Hilbert-tenth-problem project contains
corrected Jones articles and source implementations of several representation
results \cite{repo-h10}. Its merged report \emph{Canonical Diophantine
certificates} contains, among other constructions, a polynomial-trajectory
certificate whose arity is independent of the horizon and cubic in a fixed
degree parameter \cite{repo-cdc}. That polynomial case is the direct
starting point of this work. The present extension replaces ordinary finite
differences by a chain of $E-b$ operators and retains fixed-base powers in the
arithmetic language.

We do not reproduce the repository's finite memory-log, queue, routing, or
instruction-tableau constructions. Nor do we claim to improve its separate
universal-polynomial operation counts. Our contribution is a structural
compression theorem, an explicit compiler, and a precise obstruction to
eliminating its remaining power predicates while preserving witness
multiplicity.

The source file \path{Paper1984/DPR.lean} contains the declarations
\path{re_sfu} and \path{re_single_equation}. They provide the
single-fold unary exponential representation of recursively enumerable sets
\cite{repo-dpr}. This is an important existing result, not something inferred
from ordinary MRDP. We use its classical mathematical counterpart in the
boundary theorem. The source was inspected, not rebuilt during this work.

\subsubsection{Relation to the verification literature}
There is a substantial prior theory of loop termination. Tiwari studied
termination of linear loops on all initial real values \cite{tiwari}.
Hosseini, Ouaknine, and Worrell proved decidability of termination of affine
single-path loops on all integer initial values; their work carefully
distinguishes that question from termination on one specified input
\cite{how2019}. Hark, Frohn, and Giesl study triangular weakly nonlinear loops,
polynomial guards, closed forms, and linearization \cite{hfg2024}. These classes
and their closed-form analysis are not new here. The broader complexity of
exponential-polynomial zeros is illustrated by Chonev, Ouaknine, and Worrell
\cite{cow2023}.

The additional object developed here is a \emph{canonical natural-number
certificate of the complete discrete sign diagram}, including its early
transient behavior and, in the infinite version, its entire tail. Our focus
is exact witness multiplicity and horizon-independent arithmetic size, not a
new claim that known restricted loop classes are decidable. The zero-count
argument used below is a standard real-exponential Chebyshev mechanism; we
prove the needed form directly.

\subsubsection{A map of the results}
The central result is \cref{cdc:ps:thm:compiler}. Its mathematical foundation is the
local-verifier theorem, \cref{cdc:ps:thm:local}, and its main computational transfer is
\cref{cdc:ps:thm:triangular,cdc:ps:thm:phases}. \Cref{cdc:ps:thm:powbarrier} identifies the exact
single-fold and finite-fold bottleneck already in the order-two sequence
$2^n-y$. \Cref{cdc:ps:thm:rotation} limits the sign-run method for complex spectra.

The results are deliberately separated into four layers:

compiler, exported examples, and independent checks. \\

\paragraph{Abstract.}
% ---- manuscript 18, lines 90-116 ----
A long execution can have a short algebraic certificate only if its guards can
be checked without materializing its intermediate states. We study the exact
integer-time sign of
\[
 F(n)=\sum_{i=1}^{s}P_i(n)b_i^n,\qquad
 1\le b_1<\cdots<b_s,\quad P_i\in\Z[X],
\]
with declared dimension $D=\sum_i(1+\deg_{\rm declared}P_i)$. Successive
operators $E-b_i$, applied in a fixed order with multiplicity, produce a
root-removing ladder ending at zero. The lower row controls monotonicity of a
positively normalized upper row. This yields a certificate consisting of
maximal discrete sign intervals, verified only at explicitly computed
endpoints. The certificate is unique, has exactly $D^2+1$ allocated interval
slots, and uses $O(D^4)$ arithmetic gates and functional power atoms,
independently of the numerical horizon $T$.

For each fixed shape this gives a single-fold existential representation in
arithmetic augmented by $y=b^n$. For each externally fixed $B\ge1$, binary
powering yields an ordinary polynomial of degree at most four with
$O(D^4(B+1))$ natural witnesses, uniform for $T<2^B$. We give an elementary,
coefficient-explicit eventual-sign threshold, applications to guarded affine
loops with positive rational spectrum, and a second-order integer recurrence
whose sign charts grow linearly even on every fixed residue class. A worked
million-horizon example has only nine occupied ladder blocks. Tests compare
3,787 chart instances against exhaustive evaluation and independently verify
serialized equations. The size bounds count arithmetic coordinates, not their
potentially enormous bit lengths.

% ---- manuscript 18, lines 123-189 ----
\subsubsection{Why another computation certificate?}
The existence of a Diophantine representation of a computably enumerable
relation is supplied by the Davis--Putnam--Robinson--Matiyasevich theorem.
Mechanized reductions through counter machines and FRACTRAN are also already
available; Larchey-Wendling and Forster give a substantial Coq development
\cite{lf2022}. Reapplying existence alone to a differently named universal machine
would not address the principal engineering problem: which coordinates of an
execution can be omitted while retaining an exact, independently checkable
certificate?

The inspected ProveIt interface \texttt{DiophantineTrace.lean} proves closure
under bounded universal quantification, exact finite iteration, and
existentially quantified iteration length \cite{repo-trace}. Those theorems do
not assert a witness count, a height bound, or uniqueness of witnesses. The
repository's research report \emph{Canonical Diophantine certificates} goes
further. In particular, its polynomial-trajectory component constructs
horizon-independent certificates for fixed-degree polynomial guards and
applies them to unipotent and polynomially iterable updates
\cite{repo-cdc}. We extend that direction to genuine exponential
modes and their polynomial factors.

\srcnote{\wtag{} Batch~79, 2 October 2026. The research report is this one, at its pin a report of Parts~I--XIV; its polynomial-trajectory component is Part~IV, whose unipotent and polynomially iterable updates are \cref{cdc:pt:prop:unipotent,cdc:pt:thm:acceleration}. Manuscript~18 read this report's README and manuscript~02's source ledger \path{02-poly-trajectories-sources.md}, not the article (\path{18-spectral-guards-SOURCES.md}), and did not know manuscript~17, written from the same pin on the same day. The interface it names is \path{Computability/HilbertTenthProblem/Lean/Diophantine/Common/DiophantineTrace.lean} (blob \texttt{08e5796b2}, unchanged at this write). The construction question it states below is, in exponential arithmetic, Source~02 of \cref{cdc:q:compression}; see the dated note there.}


Consider an affine loop that doubles one counter and quadruples another.
Closed forms make its final state easy to express. They do not, by themselves,
justify that a guard remained true at every intervening integer time. Positive
values at both ends of an interval are insufficient: the sequence
$4^n-10\cdot2^n+16$ is positive at $n=0,4$ and negative at $n=2$. Our object is
an exact certificate for all intervening signs, rather than a heuristic
stabilization estimate or an unrolled execution tableau.

\subsubsection{The precise advance}
The central result is a combination of four ingredients: a root-removing
\emph{difference} ladder, a classical zero bound used only to bound certificate
shape, canonical maximal discrete sign charts, and a fully functional
quadratic-residual compiler. It resolves the following concrete construction
question raised by extending the repository's trajectory approach:

\begin{quote}
Can guards with several positive exponential modes and Jordan factors be
certified by a unique, explicitly bounded arithmetic witness whose number of
coordinates does not grow with the number of loop iterations?
\end{quote}

The answer is yes in exponential arithmetic; in ordinary polynomial arithmetic
we give a uniform, unique-witness quartic for every externally fixed bit bound
on the iteration count. The answer is accompanied by an exact compiler, not
just a closure argument. The allocated chart size $D^2+1$, the pair count in
Theorem~\ref{cdc:sg:thm:endpoint}, and the explicit eventual-sign threshold are useful
quantitative features. The oscillatory example in Section~\ref{cdc:sg:sec:obstruction}
identifies a sharp limitation of this particular compression mechanism.

\subsubsection{What the literature already supplies}
Positive-spectrum and triangular-loop analysis is not a new decidability
territory. Hark, Frohn, and Giesl study termination of triangular weakly
nonlinear loops through closed forms and logical reductions \cite{hfg2024}.
Frohn, Giesl, Giesl, and Lommen's 2026 work addresses constant runtime for
linear loops with real eigenvalues \cite{fggl2026}. Our theorem concerns the
\emph{format, cardinality, and uniqueness of exact certificates}; it is not a
replacement claim for these termination results.

Likewise, single-fold exponential Diophantine representations have classical
precedents. Cantone, Cuzziol, and Omodeo discuss such representations and the
care needed to preserve uniqueness under arithmetic constructions
\cite{cco2024}. The unrestricted ordinary-polynomial finite-fold and single-fold
questions are a different issue \cite{mat2010}. Finally, arbitrary recurrence
roots lead to the Skolem and Positivity landscape surveyed by Bacik and
coauthors \cite{bkl-survey}. We isolate an explicitly tractable spectral class
without claiming to solve those general problems.

\paragraph{Abstract.}
% ---- manuscript 19 (batch-79 manuscript 05), lines 64-88 ----
A nonnegative firing vector that leaves a sandpile stable need not describe
legal computation: chip-balance equations permit mutually borrowed firings.
We give a history-free arithmetic certificate that removes this ambiguity.
For a finite loopless undirected multigraph with $n$ nonsink vertices and
$E$ distinct internal adjacent pairs, an explicit system of $12n+16E$
quadratic equations in $11n+12E$ natural witnesses has exactly one solution
if legal stabilization terminates, and none otherwise. Its sum of squares
is one quartic polynomial. The essential semantic condition is a burning
test restricted to the support of the proposed odometer. Two local rank
inequalities force the \emph{simultaneous} burning rounds and hence make
all auxiliary witnesses canonical.

A no-firing boundary halo transfers the construction to finite-support
stabilization on $\Z^d$. In dimension three the same construction becomes
one radius-one, pointwise quartic identity with 47 natural-valued field
witnesses and 60 quadratic residuals. The fields have prescribed periodic
tails and only finitely many deviations. Together with Cairns's established
simulation theorem, this gives a unique-field-witness normal form for a
$\Sigma^0_1$-complete problem. It also implies that no computable input-only
bound can control the required support radius or support cardinality.
We prove an explicit height bound once a containing cube is supplied.
The package includes a coefficient-level compiler, exact finite tests, a
fully expanded example, and a research agenda. No fixed-47-integer-witness,
single-fold MRDP, arithmetic-operation optimality, or Lean-verification claim
is made.

\subsubsection{The result and its research boundary}\label{cdc:nb:sec:scope}

The question addressed here is more precise than whether a computational
substrate is Diophantine. Ordinary MRDP already represents every
computably enumerable set by an existential polynomial equation.
A useful substrate-specific compiler should instead explain what its
witnesses mean, exclude false computations, and account for every helper.
For an abelian system it is particularly natural to ask whether an entire
chronological history can be replaced by the number of actions at each
location. The obstruction is that a consistent final balance does not
necessarily admit any legal ordering of those actions.

This article resolves three concrete construction questions for undirected
sandpiles. First, it gives a local-rank, history-free certificate of the
\emph{actual} odometer, not just an upper stabilizer. Second, it makes the
whole arithmetic witness unique over the natural numbers, including
comparison branches and unused slacks. Third, it converts the construction
to a fixed number of finite-deviation fields for an established universal
sandpile class, while identifying precisely why this is not a fixed-arity
single-fold polynomial over ordinary integers.

\paragraph{Relationship to the repository}

The repository snapshot inspected for this report is
\begin{center}\texttt{e58b724c25bd34533b7a5834cfcbe873dfa01288}.\end{center}
The Hilbert-tenth-problem guide records extensive polynomial compilers,
including a maintained 87-operation universal-polynomial bound
\cite{repo-h10}. The MRDP guide specifies the natural-witness interface
\code{Diophantine.mrdp}: its conclusion is the existence of a fixed finite
integer polynomial for an enumerable set, not uniqueness of witnesses
\cite{repo-mrdp}. The existing run-length-routing source audit separates
finite rotor computations from Cairns's infinite-background sandpile
universality \cite{repo-rtsources}. That distinction is retained here.

Our counts concern \emph{variables and quadratic residuals}. They are not
arithmetic-circuit operation counts and do not improve the repository's
87-operation result. The new construction is supplied as an independent
Python module and a mathematical article. No existing repository file has
been changed, and its Lean build has not been rerun.
