\section{Queue semantics and the role of a prescribed trace\srctag{20}}
\label{cdc:cq:sec:semantics}

Throughout, $\N=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$. Fix a finite nonempty alphabet $\Sigma$.
The empty word is $\eps$, juxtaposition denotes concatenation, and $|w|$
denotes word length. The contents of a queue are written with its readable
head on the left.

\begin{definition}[Atomic queue action]
An action is a tuple
\[
 e=(p,u,v,p'), \qquad u,v\in\Sigma^*,
\]
where $p,p'$ are control states. Its partial transition is
\[
 (p,uz)\longmapsto(p',zv).
\]
The whole word $u$ is removed before any part of $v$ is appended.
There is no transition on a queue not beginning with $u$.
\end{definition}

Empty read and write words are allowed. An empty read means an append-only
action, not an emptiness test. The transition table of a queue program is
finite. The table can be nondeterministic, but a \emph{trace} specifies its
actual action labels and therefore resolves transition choices.

A finite action sequence $\tau=e_1\cdots e_T$ is
\emph{control-compatible} if the target of each action equals the source of
the next. All semantic assertions below presuppose this check. Write
$q\xrightarrow{\tau}r$ when the actions can actually be executed, starting
with queue word $q$ and ending with $r$; the control endpoints are implicit
in $\tau$. Define the total read and write words
\begin{equation}
 \readw(\tau)=u_1\cdots u_T,
 \qquad
 \writew(\tau)=v_1\cdots v_T.
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:totalwords}
\end{equation}
Their order matters. Replacing them by symbol counts would lose FIFO
information.

\subsection{Cyclic tag systems fit without a separate arithmetic model}
\srcnote{\wtag{} [Cook's cyclic-tag semantics \cite{cook}, as in Part~VI (\cref{cdc:qc:sec:stream}), where each consumed symbol is a coordinate; here the run is a supplied grammar.]}


Let $A_0,\ldots,A_{m-1}$ be binary appendants, with $m\ge1$. A configuration
is a phase $j\in\Z/m\Z$ and a binary queue. At a nonempty queue, delete the
first bit. If it is $1$, append $A_j$; if it is $0$, append nothing. Then
advance the phase. Thus phase $j$ has the two actions
\begin{equation}
 (j,0,\eps,j+1), \qquad (j,1,A_j,j+1).
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:cts}
\end{equation}
The empty queue has no successor. This explicit operational definition is
all that our certificates require. A valid trace grammar must select these
actions with matching phases; it may not select a bit independently of the
actual FIFO contents. The arithmetic endpoint test will enforce that
agreement.

A closed CTS macro has a number of actions divisible by $m$. The program's
phase cycle by itself does not imply that its sequence of read bits is
periodic. Our infinite-loop theorem concerns a repeated \emph{complete
transition trace}, including these bits.

\subsection{Why one global word identity is insufficient}

Every execution satisfies
\begin{equation}
 q\writew(\tau)=\readw(\tau)r.
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:conservation}
\end{equation}
The converse is false. Start with $q=0$ and propose the two actions
\[
 (0\text{ read},\eps\text{ written}),\qquad
 (1\text{ read},1\text{ written}).
\]
Then $\readw=01$, $\writew=1$, and
$q\writew=01=\readw\eps$. Nevertheless the first action empties the queue,
so the second is disabled. The purported computation borrows its own future
output. This example can also be placed in a two-phase cyclic tag program.

\wtag{} The same circular justification is what manuscript~19 calls a borrowed firing in an abelian sandpile (\cref{cdc:nb:ex:phantom}, inside Part~XVI), where support burning excludes it; for queues, Part~VI's self-starting fiction and its first-failure product (\cref{cdc:qc:thm:first-failure}) treat it, and here the resource threshold of \cref{cdc:cq:thm:endpoint} does.


There are two independent obstructions: the head symbols may be wrong, or
there may not yet be enough symbols. We retain global word equality to
check the first obstruction and compress the second into a length-resource
pair. The pair must describe every internal prefix of the macro, not just
its net change in queue length.

\section{Causal resource algebra and endpoint reconstruction\srctag{20}}
\label{cdc:cq:sec:resource}

\subsection{The length-only partial action}

Ignore symbol values temporarily. The length action of $e=(p,u,v,p')$ is
\[
 n\longmapsto n-|u|+|v|, \qquad n\ge |u|.
\]
A pair $(R,S)\in\N^2$ denotes the partial map
\begin{equation}
 n\longmapsto n-R+S,\qquad n\ge R.
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:resourcepair}
\end{equation}
The identity pair is $(0,0)$ and an atomic action has pair $(|u|,|v|)$.
For pairs $(R_1,S_1),(R_2,S_2)$, put
\begin{align}
 d&=\min(S_1,R_2), &
 \alpha&=S_1-d, & \beta&=R_2-d,\notag\\
 (R_1,S_1)\star(R_2,S_2)
   &=(R_1+\beta,S_2+\alpha).
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:resourcecomposition}
\end{align}

\srcnote{\wtag{} [The one-coordinate case of manuscript~06's resource product (\cref{cdc:cs:lem:resourceproduct}, Part~I): with $c=\min(S_1,R_2)$, the pair \eqref{cdc:cq:eq:resourcecomposition} is $(R_1+R_2-c,\,S_1+S_2-c)$, which is \eqref{cdc:cs:eq:product}; the direct formula \eqref{cdc:cq:eq:prefixdeficit} below is \eqref{cdc:cs:eq:prefixformula}. Manuscript~20's proof through partial length maps is kept as a second route.]}
\begin{lemma}[Exact resource composition]
\label{cdc:cq:lem:resourcecomposition}
The pair in \eqref{cdc:cq:eq:resourcecomposition} describes precisely the
composition of the two partial length maps. Consequently $\star$ is
associative, with identity $(0,0)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The first map requires $n\ge R_1$. After it, the second requires
$n-R_1+S_1\ge R_2$. Together these inequalities are
\[
 n\ge R_1+\max(0,R_2-S_1)=R_1+\beta.
\]
The final value is $n-R_1+S_1-R_2+S_2$.
Since $S_1-R_2=\alpha-\beta$, this is
$n-(R_1+\beta)+(S_2+\alpha)$. Thus the stated pair is exact.
A pair is uniquely determined by the domain threshold and the value of the
map at that threshold. Associativity of partial-map composition therefore
implies associativity of $\star$.
\end{proof}

Let $(\res(\tau),\sur(\tau))$ be the product of the atomic pairs. If
$a=|\readw(\tau)|$ and $b=|\writew(\tau)|$, then
\begin{equation}
 \sur(\tau)-\res(\tau)=b-a.
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:drift}
\end{equation}
For an unexpanded trace, the equivalent direct formula is
\begin{equation}
 \res(\tau)=\max\left(0,
  \max_{1\le i\le T}
  \left\{\sum_{j\le i}|u_j|-\sum_{j<i}|v_j|\right\}\right).
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:prefixdeficit}
\end{equation}
It uses the output \emph{before} the current action, reflecting
read-before-write semantics. In particular $0\le\res(\tau)\le a$.

\srcnote{\wtag{} [Manuscript~06's power formula (\cref{cdc:cs:thm:power}) in one coordinate, for $k\ge1$: with $c=\min(R,S)$, \eqref{cdc:cq:eq:resourcepower} is $(c+k(R-c),\,c+k(S-c))$. Second route.]}
\begin{proposition}[Powers of a resource pair]
\label{cdc:cq:prop:resourcepower}
For $k\ge1$,
\begin{equation}
 (R,S)^{\star k}=
 \bigl(R+(k-1)(R-S)_+,\ S+(k-1)(S-R)_+\bigr),
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:resourcepower}
\end{equation}
where $x_+=\max(x,0)$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Set $\delta=S-R$. At the start of copy $i$, numbering from zero,
the length is $n+i\delta$. Every copy is length-feasible exactly when
$n+i\delta\ge R$ for $0\le i<k$. If $\delta\ge0$, the strongest condition
is the first; if $\delta<0$, it is the last. The resulting threshold is
$R+(k-1)(-\delta)_+$. The final drift is $k\delta$, which gives the second
coordinate in \eqref{cdc:cq:eq:resourcepower}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The endpoint theorem}

\srcnote{\wtag{} [The one-queue case of \cref{cdc:qc:thm:network-causality} (manuscript~07, Part~VI): its word identity is \eqref{cdc:qc:eq:network-word}, and its guard $G>0$, manuscript~07's first-failure product over the steps (\cref{cdc:qc:thm:first-failure}), is replaced by the single threshold $|q|\ge\res(\tau)$, which is equivalent and composes along a grammar by \cref{cdc:cq:lem:resourcecomposition}. Kept as a second route, because \cref{cdc:cq:thm:compiler} needs the compositional form.]}
\begin{theorem}[Causal endpoint reconstruction]
\label{cdc:cq:thm:endpoint}
For a control-compatible finite trace $\tau$ and actual words $q,r$,
\begin{equation}
 q\xrightarrow{\tau}r
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 |q|\ge\res(\tau)
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 q\writew(\tau)=\readw(\tau)r.
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:endpoint}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
An execution satisfies the length condition by the exactness of the
resource pair. For one action, $q=uz$ and $r=zv$ give $qv=ur$.
Repeated substitution proves the word equality for any number of actions.

For the converse, use induction on the number of actions. The empty trace
is immediate. Write $\tau=e\sigma$, with $e$ reading $u$ and writing $v$.
Length feasibility implies $|q|\ge|u|$. In
\[
 qv\writew(\sigma)=u\readw(\sigma)r,
\]
the first $|u|$ letters of the left side therefore lie entirely in $q$.
They must equal $u$, so $q=uz$ for a word $z$. Cancel $u$ to obtain
\[
 zv\writew(\sigma)=\readw(\sigma)r.
\]
The first action is legal and leaves $zv$. Exact resource composition also
implies $|zv|\ge\res(\sigma)$. The induction hypothesis now executes
$\sigma$ from $zv$ to $r$.
\end{proof}

An important feature of this proof is what it does not do: it neither
postulates a supply of symbols outside the queue nor reconstructs a
simultaneous tableau of all intermediate words. Causality is recovered
from a global content equality together with a compositionally computed
prefix-resource threshold.

\subsection{Length summaries are not semantic normal forms}

The pair $(\res,\sur)$ is exact for lengths with symbols forgotten. Its
first coordinate need not be the length of the shortest \emph{content-
compatible} input queue. For example, append $0$ and then read $1$.
The raw resource threshold is zero, but the empty queue does not work;
the queue $1$ does.

The following formula isolates this distinction. It is included to prevent
confusing our convenient arithmetic summary with a canonical queue-monoid
normal form of the kind studied in~\cite{hkz}.

\begin{proposition}[Saturating the resource threshold by word overlap]
\label{cdc:cq:prop:saturation}
Let $U=\readw(\tau)$, $V=\writew(\tau)$, $a=|U|$, $b=|V|$, and
$R=\res(\tau)$. The minimum length of any input word on which $\tau$ is
executable equals
\begin{equation}
 H=a-\max\{t:0\le t\le\min(b,a-R),\ \suff_t(U)=\pref_t(V)\}.
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:saturated}
\end{equation}
In \eqref{cdc:cq:eq:endpoint}, replacing $|q|\ge R$ by $|q|\ge H$ preserves the
characterized relation.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
The set in \eqref{cdc:cq:eq:saturated} contains $0$. The input $U$ always works:
it has length $a\ge R$ and $UV=UV$ supplies the endpoint $V$.
Thus a minimum input length is at most $a$.

Consider an input of length $a-t\le a$. The word equation forces that input
to be $\pref_{a-t}(U)$. The missing suffix of $U$ must then come from the
beginning of $V$, giving $\suff_t(U)=\pref_t(V)$. The residual word exists
exactly when $t\le b$, while length feasibility requires $t\le a-R$.
Conversely these conditions give the required endpoint equation, with the
residual obtained by deleting the first $t$ symbols of $V$, and the endpoint
theorem makes the trace executable. Maximizing $t$ minimizes the input
length. No executable input can have length below $H$, and every input
satisfying the strengthened condition still satisfies $|q|\ge R$.
\end{proof}

Our compiler deliberately retains the simpler raw threshold $R$. It is
compositional using only addition and a single minimum. Computing the
semantic threshold $H$ is unnecessary for soundness, completeness, or
unique arithmetic witnesses.

\section{Arithmetic encodings with no auxiliary ambiguity\srctag{20}}
\label{cdc:cq:sec:arith}

\subsection{Radix pairs}

Choose an injective digit map $d:\Sigma\to\{1,\ldots,s\}$ where
$s=|\Sigma|$, and put $B=s+1$. Define
\begin{equation}
 \scale(w)=B^{|w|},\qquad
 \qval(w)=\sum_{i=1}^{|w|}d(w_i)B^{|w|-i}.
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:radix}
\end{equation}
In particular $(\scale(\eps),\qval(\eps))=(1,0)$.
Although the chosen nonzero digits already avoid leading-zero ambiguity,
we retain both scale and value because concatenation then has a bilinear
formula:
\begin{equation}
 \scale(uv)=\scale(u)\scale(v),\qquad
 \qval(uv)=\qval(u)\scale(v)+\qval(v).
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:radixconcat}
\end{equation}
These identities follow directly by splitting the positional sum.
The pair $(\scale,\qval)$ is injective: equality of scales gives equal
lengths, and uniqueness of fixed-length radix expansions gives equal
symbols. For completeness, the latter uniqueness follows by taking both
values modulo $B$ to recover the last digit, subtracting that digit,
dividing by $B$, and inducting on the length.

Input and output pairs in this article always encode \emph{actual words}.
An arbitrary triple of natural numbers labelled ``length, scale, value''
need not encode a word. The polynomial theorem below is either read with
actual words supplied, or with valid encodings as an explicit hypothesis.
No unnoticed Diophantine definition of ``is a power of $B$'' is being used.
Internal word pairs are valid because their leaves are fixed valid pairs
and their only operation is concatenation.

\subsection{A single-fold minimum gadget}
\srcnote{\wtag{} [Manuscript~06's unique minimum gadget (\cref{cdc:cs:lem:min}), with the same three equations.]}


For prescribed $x,y\in\N$, introduce $d,\alpha,\beta\in\N$ and impose
\begin{equation}
 x=d+\alpha,\qquad y=d+\beta,\qquad\alpha\beta=0.
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:mingadget}
\end{equation}
These equations have exactly one solution:
\[
 d=\min(x,y),\quad \alpha=(x-y)_+,\quad\beta=(y-x)_+.
\]
Indeed, if $x\le y$ and $\alpha>0$, the product equation gives $\beta=0$,
whence $d=y$ and $x=y+\alpha>y$, a contradiction. Thus $\alpha=0$ and all
coordinates are determined. The other case is symmetric. This includes
$x=y$, when both excesses are zero.

The domain $\N$ is important. Over all integers, the same equations do not
characterize the minimum. Likewise replacing a nonnegative slack by a
sum-of-four-squares representation would usually introduce multiple
witnesses. We keep natural-number variables and do not make an
integer-domain uniqueness claim.

\subsection{From quadratic residuals to one quartic}

If $F_1,\ldots,F_M$ are integer polynomials of degree at most two, then
\begin{equation}
 Q=\sum_{j=1}^{M}F_j^2
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:sos}
\end{equation}
has degree at most four, and $Q=0$ over $\N$ is equivalent to
$F_j=0$ for every $j$. There are no new variables in this conversion.
We say that this is a \emph{unique-witness} or \emph{single-fold}
certificate for the specified parameters when its zero set in $\N^N$
is empty or a singleton. This local terminology is not a claim about
single-fold representations of every computably enumerable relation.

\section{The grammar-size quartic compiler\srctag{20}}
\label{cdc:cq:sec:compiler}

\subsection{Straight-line trace grammars}

A grammar is a topologically ordered list of nodes $X_1,\ldots,X_g$.
A leaf contains a fixed action; an internal node has the form
$X_i=X_jX_k$ with $j,k<i$. The root is $X_g$. Both children may be the same
node, and a node may be shared by many parents. There are $l$ leaves and
$c$ concatenations, with $g=l+c$.

The control endpoints of every node are computed statically. A leaf has
its action's endpoints. A concatenation is permitted precisely when its
left target equals its right source. A syntactically malformed or
control-incompatible grammar can be rejected at compilation time, or
represented by the constant polynomial $1$.

An empty trace can be handled separately by the identity relation $q=r$.
Alternatively, an explicitly identified identity leaf can carry summary
$(1,0,1,0,0,0)$ at a prescribed control state. An actual append-only action
with an empty read must not be confused with a halting convention.

\subsection{Coordinates and residuals}

For every node $i$, allocate six natural-number coordinates
\[
 (P_i^U,C_i^U,P_i^V,C_i^V,R_i,S_i).
\]
They are intended to equal the encodings of its total read and write words
and its resource pair. At a leaf with action $(p,u,v,p')$, impose the six
linear equations fixing these coordinates to
\begin{equation}
 (\scale(u),\qval(u),\scale(v),\qval(v),|u|,|v|).
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:leaf}
\end{equation}

At a concatenation $X_i=X_jX_k$, allocate three more natural coordinates
$d_i,\alpha_i,\beta_i$. Impose the four word equations
\begin{align}
 P_i^U-P_j^UP_k^U&=0,&
 C_i^U-C_j^UP_k^U-C_k^U&=0,\notag\\
 P_i^V-P_j^VP_k^V&=0,&
 C_i^V-C_j^VP_k^V-C_k^V&=0,
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:nodeword}
\end{align}
and the five resource equations
\begin{align}
 S_j-d_i-\alpha_i&=0,&
 R_k-d_i-\beta_i&=0,&
 \alpha_i\beta_i&=0,\notag\\
 R_i-R_j-\beta_i&=0,&
 S_i-S_k-\alpha_i&=0.
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:noderesource}
\end{align}
All nine residuals have degree at most two.

Finally, for prescribed queue words $q,r$, allocate one slack $z\in\N$.
Writing $P_q=\scale(q)$, $C_q=\qval(q)$ and similarly for $r$, impose
\begin{align}
 P_qP_g^V-P_g^UP_r&=0,\notag\\
 C_qP_g^V+C_g^V-C_g^UP_r-C_r&=0,\notag\\
 |q|-R_g-z&=0.
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:root}
\end{align}
The first two equations assert equality of the encodings of $qV$ and $Ur$;
the third supplies causality. Here the supplied word encodings are
coefficients, not unknown internally generated scales.

\begin{theorem}[Exact unique-witness quartic compilation]
\label{cdc:cq:thm:compiler}
For every control-compatible straight-line trace grammar $G$ and actual
queue words $q,r$, equations \eqref{cdc:cq:eq:leaf}--\eqref{cdc:cq:eq:root} yield an
explicit polynomial $Q_{G,q,r}\in\Z[\mathbf x]$ of degree at most four
such that
\[
 \#\{\mathbf x\in\N^N:Q_{G,q,r}(\mathbf x)=0\}
 =\begin{cases}
 1,&q\xrightarrow{\operatorname{val}(G)}r,\\
 0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
The exact numbers of variables and residuals are
\begin{equation}
 N=6g+3c+1,\qquad M=6l+9c+3.
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:counts}
\end{equation}
In particular $N\le9g+1$ and $M\le9g+3$. No intermediate queue word is
quantified.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Form $Q$ by summing the squares of all listed residuals. Its degree bound
is immediate. At each leaf, all six variables are fixed uniquely.
Assume the variables of nodes before $i$ are fixed to their intended
summaries. At a concatenation, \eqref{cdc:cq:eq:nodeword} fixes the four word
coordinates by radix concatenation. The minimum gadget uniquely fixes
$d_i,\alpha_i,\beta_i$, and \eqref{cdc:cq:eq:noderesource} then fixes $R_i,S_i$
to the exact composite resource pair. Induction determines every node and
all its auxiliary variables uniquely, even when children are shared.

With these values fixed, the first two root equations are equivalent to
$qV=Ur$, by validity and injectivity of the word encodings. The final root
equation has a natural solution exactly when $|q|\ge R_g$, and that
solution is uniquely $z=|q|-R_g$. The endpoint theorem proves both
soundness and completeness. If the execution exists, every intended
coordinate and slack is natural and satisfies its residual, so there is
one zero. If it does not, the uniquely determined node data cannot satisfy
all root equations, so there is none.

There are six variables at each of $g$ nodes, three at each of $c$
concatenations, and one at the root. There are six residuals at each leaf,
nine at each concatenation, and three at the root. This proves the counts.
\end{proof}

\subsection{What the size assertion means}

Each residual has a bounded number of monomials. Squaring and adding
therefore produces a sparse polynomial with $O(g)$ monomials, before or
after merging equal terms. Repeated subexpressions in the computation do
not become repeated blocks of variables: one shared grammar node has one
summary.

For a fixed transition table, leaf coefficients have bounded bit length.
The root coefficients have bit length $O(|q|+|r|)$ for a fixed alphabet.
The grammar itself needs $O(g\log(g+1))$ bits to identify child indices.
Thus the theorem controls variable count, degree, sparse algebraic size,
and coefficient size separately. It does \emph{not} bound the bit lengths
of a satisfying assignment polynomially in $g$.

The construction is not optimized by eliminating leaf variables or
redundant equations. Retaining them makes the exact count independent of
ad hoc simplifications and makes the induction directly mirror the grammar.
One can remove fixed coordinates by substitution, but the reported counts
refer to the uneliminated, reproducible compiler.

\paragraph{\wtag{} The contract of \cref{cdc:cs:prop:abstract}.} The six coordinates $(P^U,C^U,P^V,C^V,R,S)$ are an exact finite summary of a reliable FIFO trace, and \eqref{cdc:cq:eq:nodeword}--\eqref{cdc:cq:eq:noderesource} compose them by unique quadratic gadgets, so FIFO actions satisfy manuscript~06's unique-summary contract under concatenation. For arbitrary powers they do not stay polynomial: \cref{cdc:cq:thm:powered} keeps explicit power predicates, which is the obstruction for word-valued summaries that the contract's discussion anticipates. Fixed powers compile by binary concatenation (\cref{cdc:cq:sec:infinitequartic}). This answers the queue clause of \cref{cdc:q:storage}; see the note there.

\paragraph{\wtag{} A projection by the research tree.} Batch~79, 2 October 2026. The research tree's review of this archive \cite{repo-cqrev} verifies a projection of the finite compiler with $6c+1$ natural coordinates and $6c+3$ quadratic residuals. The six leaf coordinates become constants; an internal node keeps its four word coordinates and $\alpha_i,\beta_i$, with $R_i=R_j+\beta_i$, $S_i=S_k+\alpha_i$ defined recursively and $d_i=S_j-\alpha_i$ restored; the rows $R_k-S_j+\alpha_i-\beta_i=0$ and $\alpha_i\beta_i=0$ replace the three minimum rows; the root keeps its slack and three rows. Substituting the restoration into the original sum of squares gives the new one identically on every integer tuple, and the restored cancellation values are natural at natural zeros, so the two have the same natural zeros. The review claims no reduction of arithmetic operations, and affine resource expansion can enlarge the sparse size.


\section{Worked finite examples and exponential compression\srctag{20}}
\label{cdc:cq:sec:examples}

\subsection{A binary macro that works twice and then fails}

Use binary digits $d(0)=1$, $d(1)=2$, so $B=3$. Let
\[
 e_0:\text{read }0,\ \text{append }010,
 \qquad e_1:\text{read }1,\ \text{append }\eps.
\]
Both may be given the same control state in a general queue program.
Set $X_1=e_0$, $X_2=e_1$, $X_3=X_1X_2$, $X_4=X_3X_3$.
Thus $g=4$, $l=2$, $c=2$, and the root describes four actions.
The summaries are
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{crrrrrr}
\toprule
Node & $P^U$ & $C^U$ & $P^V$ & $C^V$ & $R$ & $S$\\
\midrule
$X_1$ & 3 & 1 & 27 & 16 & 1 & 3\\
$X_2$ & 3 & 2 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 0\\
$X_3$ & 9 & 5 & 27 & 16 & 1 & 2\\
$X_4$ & 81 & 50 & 729 & 448 & 1 & 3\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Starting with $q=01$, one macro $e_0e_1$ gives $010$, and a second gives
$r=0010$. The root conservation equation is
\[
 01\,010010=0101\,0010.
\]
The root slack is $|q|-R=1$. The compiled polynomial has $31$ variables,
$33$ residuals, degree four, and, after collection, $98$ nonzero monomials.
Its full sparse representation and its unique natural witness are included
in \path{data/20-compressed-queue-example_quartic.json}.

A third macro fails on its second action. The exact repetition theorem
below will detect that failure without simulating the intermediate queues.
Notice also that the queue is growing overall: nonnegative length drift
alone does not guarantee indefinite repeatability.

\subsection{A repeated trace with an exponential expansion}

Consider the single-phase cyclic tag program whose appendant is $1$, and
its action $e$ reading and writing $1$. Starting with queue $1$, every
copy of $e$ leaves queue $1$. Define
\[
 G_0=e,\qquad G_{i+1}=G_iG_i.
\]
The root $G_k$ expands to $T=2^k$ actions, while the grammar has $g=k+1$
nodes, one leaf, and $c=k$ concatenations. The compiler therefore uses
\begin{equation}
 N=9k+7,\qquad M=9k+9.
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:doublingcounts}
\end{equation}
Every node has resource pair $(1,1)$. At its root,
\[
 P^U=P^V=3^{2^k},\qquad C^U=C^V=3^{2^k}-1.
\]
For $k=16$, the implementation checks $65{,}536$ steps through a
$17$-node grammar and a polynomial with $151$ variables and $153$
residuals, without expanding the trace. The root scale has $103{,}873$
binary digits. This last figure is crucial: the small polynomial dimension
has not made the natural-number witness small in binary notation.

\subsection{Avoiding false conclusions from these examples}

The doubling example is intentionally elementary so that its witness can
be checked independently. Its relevance is the compression mechanism, not
any computational difficulty of that particular program. The theorem
applies to arbitrary valid trace grammars over the fixed action table;
it is not restricted to homogeneous repetitions.

Conversely, the grammar is supplied rather than automatically discovered.
A long computation need not have a small grammar. Theoretical limits on
such discovery are proved in Section~\ref{cdc:cq:sec:limits}. Replacing an
arbitrary execution by a compressed grammar is not a free step in a
complexity argument.

\section{Exact acceleration of a repeated queue macro\srctag{20}}
\label{cdc:cq:sec:repeat}

Fix a nonempty, control-compatible macro $\tau$ whose initial and final
control states agree. Write
\[
 U=\readw(\tau),\quad V=\writew(\tau),\quad
 a=|U|,\quad b=|V|,\quad R=\res(\tau),\quad S=\sur(\tau).
\]
For now assume $a>0$. Let the initial queue be $q$, with $L=|q|$.
The notation $w^\omega$ denotes the one-sided infinite periodic word
$www\cdots$ when $w\ne\eps$.

\subsection{Separating resource failure from content failure}

Define the extended match length
\begin{equation}
 M=\begin{cases}
  \lcp(qV^\omega,U^\omega),&b>0,\\
  \lcp(q,U^\omega),&b=0.
 \end{cases}
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:matchlength}
\end{equation}
It lies in $\N\cup\{\infty\}$. In the second line the first word is finite,
so $M\le L$; reaching its end counts as the end of the common prefix.

The maximum number of copies allowed by lengths alone is
\begin{equation}
 N_{\rm len}=\begin{cases}
 0,&L<R,\\
 \infty,&L\ge R\text{ and }b\ge a,\\
 1+\left\lfloor\dfrac{L-R}{a-b}\right\rfloor,
     &L\ge R\text{ and }b<a.
 \end{cases}
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:nlength}
\end{equation}
We use $\lfloor\infty/a\rfloor=\infty$.

\begin{theorem}[Exact maximum number of complete macro copies]
\label{cdc:cq:thm:maxrepeat}
The number $N_{\max}$ of executable whole copies of $\tau$ is exactly
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\displaystyle
 N_{\max}=\min\left(N_{\rm len},\left\lfloor\frac{M}{a}\right\rfloor\right).}
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:maxrepeat}
\end{equation}
Here $N_{\max}=\infty$ means that every finite number of copies is
executable, and hence the infinite repetition is an actual run.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The trace $\tau^n$ has total words $U^n,V^n$ and resource threshold
\[
 R_n=R+(n-1)(a-b)_+,\qquad n\ge1.
\]
Thus its resource condition is precisely $n\le N_{\rm len}$.
When this condition holds, the available total length after $n$ copies
is nonnegative: $L+nb-na\ge0$, since it equals the final value of the
length-only partial action.

For $b>0$, the finite word $qV^n$ is a prefix of $qV^\omega$ and has
length at least $na$. The endpoint theorem says that some final word
exists exactly when $U^n$ is a prefix of $qV^n$. This is equivalent to
$na\le M$. For $b=0$, the same argument uses $q$ instead of $qV^\omega$.
Every successful $n$ has a unique residual queue obtained by deleting its
first $na$ symbols from $qV^n$.

Both conditions describe initial segments of the possible copy counts.
Their intersection has endpoint \eqref{cdc:cq:eq:maxrepeat}. If all finite
prefixes are executable, their uniquely determined successive states fit
together to form the infinite repeated run.
\end{proof}

The formula gives the first failed \emph{macro}, not necessarily the first
failed action inside that macro. That action can subsequently be located
by checking prefixes of the macro, using the endpoint theorem and the
same grammar structure.

\subsection{A finite conjugacy criterion for infinite repetition}

\begin{theorem}[Infinite repeatability as a finite word equation]
\label{cdc:cq:thm:conjugacy}
Assume $a>0$. Let $d=\gcd(a,b)$ when $b>0$. Then the following are
equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=9mm]
\item $\tau$ can be repeated indefinitely from $q$;
\item $L\ge R$, $b\ge a$, and $qV^\omega=U^\omega$;
\item $L\ge R$, $b\ge a$, and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\displaystyle U^{b/d}q=qV^{a/d}.}
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:conjugacy}
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
The condition $b\ge a>0$ ensures that $d$ and both powers in (iii) are
well-defined and positive.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The equivalence of (i) and (ii) follows from Theorem~\ref{cdc:cq:thm:maxrepeat}:
negative drift eventually exhausts a finite queue, and with nonnegative
drift only the initial resource guard and complete stream agreement remain.

Suppose (ii), and put $\ell=ab/d$. The words $U^{b/d}q$ and $qV^{a/d}$
have the same length $\ell+L$. The second is a prefix of $qV^\omega=U^\omega$.
The first is also a prefix of $U^\omega$, because its first block has length
$\ell$, a multiple of $a$, and $q$ is a prefix of $U^\omega$.
Therefore the two words are equal.

Conversely, set $A=U^{b/d}$ and $B=V^{a/d}$. From $Aq=qB$, induction gives
$A^nq=qB^n$ for every $n\ge1$. Given any finite prefix length $h$, choose
$n$ large enough that $|A^n|\ge h$ and $|qB^n|\ge h$. The first $h$
symbols of these equal words are the first $h$ symbols of $U^\omega$ and
$qV^\omega$, respectively. Hence the infinite words agree.
\end{proof}

The condition is sensitive to the queue phase. It is not sufficient that
$U$ and $V$ merely be powers of conjugate words: the actual prefix $q$
must align the two streams as in \eqref{cdc:cq:eq:conjugacy}. Nor does indefinite
repeatability require a repeated queue configuration. For the action
reading $1$ and appending $11$, starting from $1$, the queues after whole
copies are $1^{n+1}$, which are all distinct.

\subsection{Read-free macros}

If $a=0$, each read word in the macro is empty. Every action is then
append-only (or changes only the control state). A closed macro is
executable indefinitely from every queue. It has the trivial affirmative
certificate: the zero polynomial in zero variables. The negative-drift and
periodicity analyses are neither necessary nor applicable in this case.
Keeping it separate avoids meaningless expressions such as division by
$a$ or the infinite word $\eps^\omega$.

\section{A finite pumping test and its sharp example\srctag{20}}
\label{cdc:cq:sec:fw}

For self-containment, we give the two-period fact behind the finite test.
This is the classical Fine--Wilf theorem, not a new periodicity theorem;
Rankin discusses its history and generalizations\cite{rankin}.

\begin{lemma}[Fine--Wilf, two-period form]
\label{cdc:cq:lem:fw}
Let $A,B$ be one-sided infinite words with positive periods $a,b$.
If their first $a+b-\gcd(a,b)$ symbols agree, then $A=B$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
We first prove that a finite word $w$ of length at least $a+b-d$, where
$d=\gcd(a,b)$, having both periods $a$ and $b$, also has period $d$.
It suffices to use its prefix of length exactly $a+b-d$ and then extend
using one of the known periods. Induct on $a+b$, interchanging the periods
if necessary. If $a=b$, the assertion is immediate.

Suppose $a<b$ and let $w'$ be the prefix obtained by deleting the final
$a$ positions. Its length is $b-d$. It has period $a$ and also period
$b-a$: whenever both positions in question occur, the two known periods
give
\[
 w_i=w_{i+b}=w_{i+b-a}.
\]
The middle index lies in $w$; the two outside indices lie in $w'$.
Since $\gcd(a,b-a)=d$ and
$|w'|=a+(b-a)-d$, the induction hypothesis gives period $d$ on $w'$.
Moreover $b-d\ge a$, because the positive difference $b-a$ is a multiple
of $d$. Thus $w'$ contains the first $a$ positions of $w$. Period $a$,
which is a multiple of $d$, extends their $d$-periodic pattern to all of
$w$. This proves the finite assertion.

Now the common prefix of $A,B$ has both periods and therefore period $d$.
Its length is at least $\max(a,b)$, so it contains complete period blocks
for both infinite words. Both infinite continuations are the same
$d$-periodic word.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite pumping threshold]
\label{cdc:cq:thm:pump}
Suppose $0<a\le b$, let $d=\gcd(a,b)$, and define
\begin{equation}
 K=\left\lceil\frac{L+a+b-d}{a}\right\rceil.
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:pumpingK}
\end{equation}
Then $\tau^K$ is executable from $q$ if and only if $\tau$ is executable
indefinitely from $q$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Only the forward implication needs proof. Successful execution of $K$
copies implies $L\ge R$ and that $qV^\omega$ and $U^\omega$ agree for at
least $Ka\ge L+a+b-d$ positions. In particular $q$ is the length-$L$
prefix of $U^\omega$. After this prefix, the two words being compared are
$V^\omega$ and the shift of $U^\omega$ by $L$ positions. Their periods
are $b$ and $a$, and they agree for at least $a+b-d$ symbols. By
Lemma~\ref{cdc:cq:lem:fw}, they agree forever. The infinite-repeatability
criterion now applies.
\end{proof}

There is no claim that \eqref{cdc:cq:eq:pumpingK} is the smallest possible $K$
for every macro and input. Symbol structure or a large resource
requirement can improve it. It does, however, inherit the sharp
period-comparison obstruction, and the following queue instance attains
the stated whole-macro threshold.

\begin{example}[Two successes before the decisive third test]
For the macro in Section~\ref{cdc:cq:sec:examples}, take $q=01$. Then
\[
 U=01,\quad V=010,\quad a=2,\quad b=3,\quad L=2,\quad R=1.
\]
The two streams agree for exactly five symbols:
\[
 U^\omega=01010101\cdots,\qquad
 qV^\omega=01010010\cdots.
\]
Therefore $M=5$ and $N_{\max}=\lfloor5/2\rfloor=2$.
Formula~\eqref{cdc:cq:eq:pumpingK} gives $K=3$, and this third test does fail.
After removing the initial $q$, the period-two and period-three streams
agree for three positions but not four; $a+b-d=4$.
\end{example}

\wtag{} These are the queue counterparts of Part~XII's results for priority arithmetic: the exact repetition capacity (\cref{cdc:pf:thm:capacity}), the sharp pumping bound $2H+1$ (\cref{cdc:pf:thm:pumping}) and infinite periodic instruction tails (\cref{cdc:pf:thm:infinite}). The macro and its segmentation are supplied here, as there.


\subsection{Computing the exact match length}

For explicit words, $M$ can be computed without generating the run.
Compare $q$ with the first $L$ symbols of $U^\omega$. If a mismatch occurs,
its index is $M$. Otherwise, if $b=0$, return $M=L$. If $b>0$, compare
$V^\omega$ with the shift of $U^\omega$ for only $a+b-\gcd(a,b)$ further
positions. A mismatch gives $M$; absence of a mismatch gives $M=\infty$
by Fine--Wilf.

This uses $O(L+a+b)$ symbol comparisons and an integer gcd computation.
The subsequent formula for $N_{\max}$ uses elementary integer arithmetic.
This is an explicit single-input specialization of the broader queue-loop
acceleration literature\cite{kocher}, rather than a claim that acceleration
was previously unavailable.

\section{Ordinary quartic certificates for compressed infinite loops\srctag{20}}
\label{cdc:cq:sec:infinitequartic}

The infinite word in Theorem~\ref{cdc:cq:thm:conjugacy} disappears in its finite
word equation. More importantly, the exponents $b/d$ and $a/d$ are
\emph{fixed by the supplied grammar}; they are not quantified unknowns.
Consequently they can be compiled by binary concatenation, without invoking
MRDP or adding a power predicate.

For $m\ge1$, let
\begin{equation}
 h(m)=\lfloor\log_2m\rfloor+\operatorname{popcount}(m)-1.
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:chainlength}
\end{equation}
Left-to-right binary exponentiation constructs $w^m$ using exactly $h(m)$
word concatenations: start with $w$, square for each subsequent binary
digit, and concatenate another $w$ for each digit equal to one.
In particular $h(1)=0$ and $h(m)\le2\lfloor\log_2m\rfloor$.

Each word-concatenation gate needs only two new natural variables,
$P,C$, and the two residuals
\[
 P-P_1P_2=0,\qquad C-C_1P_2-C_2=0.
\]
Unlike a trace-concatenation gate, it carries no control or resource data.

\begin{theorem}[Single-fold quartics for supplied infinite loops]
\label{cdc:cq:thm:infinitequartic}
Let $G$ be a control-compatible trace grammar with $g$ nodes, $l$ leaves,
$c$ concatenations, and closed root macro $\tau$. Let $q$ be an actual
initial queue word. Assume $0<a\le b$, with notation as above, and set
\[
 H=h(b/d)+h(a/d),\qquad d=\gcd(a,b).
\]
There is an explicit ordinary integer polynomial $I_{G,q}$ of degree at
most four, with
\begin{equation}
 N_\infty=6g+3c+2H+1,
 \qquad M_\infty=6l+9c+2H+3,
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:infinitecounts}
\end{equation}
natural variables and quadratic residuals, respectively. Its natural zero
set is a singleton if $\tau$ can repeat indefinitely from $q$, and is empty
otherwise. For a fixed action table both counts are $O(g)$; the bit
cost of the supplied word's coefficients is separate.

If $a=0$, the result is represented by the constant $0$ in zero variables.
If $a>0$ and $b<a$, it is represented by the constant $1$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Keep all node residuals of the finite compiler, but omit its three root
residuals and root slack. Add the two binary concatenation circuits for
$U^{b/d}$ and $V^{a/d}$, reusing the root's word pairs as their inputs.
Let their output pairs be $(P_A,C_A)$ and $(P_B,C_B)$.
Introduce one natural slack $z$ and impose
\begin{align}
 P_AP_q-P_qP_B&=0,\notag\\
 C_AP_q+C_q-C_qP_B-C_B&=0,\notag\\
 L-R_g-z&=0.
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:infiniteroot}
\end{align}
The first two equations are exactly the radix equality $Aq=qB$.
Theorem~\ref{cdc:cq:thm:conjugacy} proves their semantic adequacy together with
the resource guard. The node summaries, all power-circuit coordinates,
and finally the slack are uniquely determined. Summing squares gives the
quartic, and direct counting gives \eqref{cdc:cq:eq:infinitecounts}.

For the asymptotic size assertion, let $w$ bound the total-read and
-total-write lengths of a single action, replacing $w$ by $\max(1,w)$.
A binary grammar with $g$ topologically ordered nodes expands to at most
$2^{g-1}$ leaves. Thus $a,b\le w2^{g-1}$, so
$H=O(g+\log w)$. For a fixed action table $w$ is fixed. All power gates
are ordinary quadratic equations: no exponentiation relation is hidden
in their syntax. The two degenerate cases were established above.
\end{proof}

The exact bound can be displayed without asymptotic notation as
\[
 N_\infty\le9g+4\lfloor\log_2(b/d)\rfloor
                    +4\lfloor\log_2(a/d)\rfloor+1.
\]
The gcd and the binary exponents are compile-time computations on word
lengths, which are computable from the grammar by additions. Their binary
lengths are small even when the word values themselves are enormous.

\subsection{A nine-variable growing-queue certificate}

For the single action reading $1$ and appending $11$, the root summary is
\[
 (P^U,C^U,P^V,C^V,R,S)=(3,2,9,8,1,2).
\]
Here $a=1$, $b=2$, $d=1$ and $H=h(2)+h(1)=1$.
The infinite compiler therefore uses nine variables and eleven residuals.
The one extra word gate computes $U^2=11$. For a valid input encoding
$(L,P_q,C_q)$, the conjugacy content equation reduces to
\[
 8P_q+C_q=9C_q+8,
\]
that is, $C_q=P_q-1$, while the guard is $L\ge1$.
With the chosen digit convention, these are exactly the nonempty words
consisting only of $1$s. Starting at any such word, the specified read-$1$
macro grows the queue forever. The exported example uses $q=1$ and is
included as \path{data/20-compressed-queue-infinite_growth_quartic.json}.

This is a certificate for the \emph{specified macro}. It is not a complete
classification of every possible run of a larger program containing that
action. A finite nonperiodic prefix may first be needed to reach a queue
on which the macro repeats.

\wtag{} A sound certificate of nontermination for runs that never repeat a configuration. The neighbouring report \emph{liveness-beyond-halting} certifies finite-region lassos (its Proposition \texttt{lbh:qd:prop:lasso}) and remarks that lassos are not complete for unbounded counter systems; \cref{cdc:cq:thm:nolassocomplete} below is the queue form of that remark.


\subsection{Compressed lassos}

A lasso consists of a finite prefix trace, a specified entry queue word,
and a nonempty closed macro to be repeated thereafter. Compile the finite
prefix with its two endpoints, and compile the infinite macro at the entry
queue. Rename the two sets of internal variables to be disjoint and add
their quartics. The result is still a degree-at-most-four polynomial, and
its zero is unique precisely when the proposed lasso is valid.

The entry queue must be an actual supplied word, possibly supplied by its
own straight-line word grammar. Treating arbitrary unconstrained numbers
as its length and encoding would invalidate this argument. If an entry
word grammar is supplied, compile its concatenation gates as well; their
coordinates are uniquely fixed by its leaves. The total arithmetic size
is linear in these supplied grammar sizes for a fixed action table.

A valid lasso is a genuine nontermination proof for deterministic queue
computation. It is not promised that every divergent run has such a lasso;
Section~\ref{cdc:cq:sec:limits} proves that no such promise can hold for a universal
machine.

\section{Powered schemas and the exact quasi-Diophantine boundary\srctag{20}}
\label{cdc:cq:sec:powered}

A straight-line grammar describes a fixed finite word. It is often useful
to describe a family of traces by a schema containing a node $Y=X^k$,
where $k$ is an externally supplied positive natural parameter. Nested
powers and shared subexpressions are allowed. The operand of a power node
is required to have matching control endpoints, so that every positive
number of copies is control-compatible. We use $k\ge1$ throughout; allowing
zero requires explicit identity and branch conventions.

\subsection{Word powers with uniquely determined geometric sums}

Suppose $(P,C)$ encodes a nonempty word $w$. Then $P>1$, and
\begin{equation}
 P'=P^k,\qquad
 (P-1)G=P'-1,\qquad C'=CG
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:wordpower}
\end{equation}
uniquely determines
\[
 G=1+P+\cdots+P^{k-1},
 \qquad (P',C')=(\scale(w^k),\qval(w^k)).
\]
This follows by multiplying the geometric sum by $P-1$ and by repeated
radix concatenation. The quotient is a natural number and is unique because
$P-1$ is positive.

There is a genuine exceptional case. If $w=\eps$, then $P=1$, $C=0$;
the middle equation in \eqref{cdc:cq:eq:wordpower} would read $0=0$ and leave
$G$ unconstrained. For empty words we instead use just
\begin{equation}
 P'=1,\qquad C'=0,
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:emptypower}
\end{equation}
with no geometric-sum variable. In a fixed schema with only positive
powers, emptiness of the total read and total write words is determined
statically: concatenate empty words only when both operands are empty;
a positive power is empty precisely when its operand is empty.
Thus this case distinction introduces no unknown Boolean choices.

\subsection{Resources at a power node}

For the operand pair $(R,S)$, introduce three natural variables
$d,\alpha,\beta$ and impose
\begin{equation}
 S=d+\alpha,\qquad R=d+\beta,\qquad\alpha\beta=0.
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:powermin}
\end{equation}
Then impose
\begin{equation}
 R'=R+(k-1)\beta,
 \qquad S'=S+(k-1)\alpha.
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:powerresource}
\end{equation}
Proposition~\ref{cdc:cq:prop:resourcepower} proves that these are the exact
resource coordinates of the repeated macro. All five residuals have
degree at most two, even when $k$ is regarded as an input indeterminate.

\begin{definition}[The quasi-Diophantine language used here]
A formula is \emph{quasi-Diophantine} here if it is an existential
conjunction of integer polynomial equations over $\N$ and explicitly
identified predicates
\[
 \Pow(x,k,y)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y=x^k.
\]
This is a definition of the language, not a claim that a written power is
already a polynomial term. All power exponents in the schema are supplied
positive parameters.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Linear-size unique witnesses for powered schemas]
\label{cdc:cq:thm:powered}
For a fixed control-compatible powered trace schema with $g$ total nodes,
fixed actual queue endpoints, and fixed supplied positive exponents, there
is a quasi-Diophantine certificate whose natural solution set is a
singleton exactly when the instantiated trace executes between those
endpoints, and is empty otherwise. It uses at most $11g+1$ auxiliary
natural variables, at most $9g+3$ polynomial residuals of degree at most
two, and at most two $\Pow$ predicates per power node.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Leaves and concatenations are compiled as before. At a power node allocate
six output summary coordinates and the three variables from
\eqref{cdc:cq:eq:powermin}. For each nonempty total word, allocate one geometric
sum variable, use one $\Pow$ predicate, and impose the two polynomial
residuals in \eqref{cdc:cq:eq:wordpower} other than the power predicate.
For an empty total word use \eqref{cdc:cq:eq:emptypower} instead.

The node therefore uses at most eleven variables, five resource residuals,
and four word residuals. Every $\Pow$ predicate is functional in its base
and exponent. The nonempty geometric sum is unique, the empty-word branch
has no sum variable, and the resource minimum is unique. Induction over
the schema determines all summary coordinates uniquely for fixed exponents.
The usual three root residuals and one slack then establish the stated
semantics and uniqueness by the endpoint theorem.
\end{proof}

One may sum the squares of the polynomial residuals, but the resulting
quartic must still be accompanied by its $\Pow$ predicates. Omitting this
qualification would be a false degree claim about the entire formula.

\wtag{} The predicate $\Pow$ is the exact power atom of Part~XVII (\cref{cdc:conv:b79-XVII}), with variable base and exponent, and its elimination at the level of existence is Part~IX's exponentiation boundary (\cref{cdc:pt:prop:exponential-boundary}). Manuscript~20 writes it in sans-serif type; it is printed with this report's \verb|\Pow|.


\subsection{Three distinct meanings of power compression}

It is useful to distinguish three situations.
\paragraph{Fixed binary exponent.}
If each exponent is a specified integer, replace its power node by binary
concatenation gates. The result is an ordinary quartic with additional
size $O(\log(k+1))$ per power node. Its witnesses remain unique.
\paragraph{Variable exponent, power predicate retained.}
Theorem~\ref{cdc:cq:thm:powered} applies with size independent of the numerical
values of the parameters. The representation is explicitly
quasi-Diophantine and single-fold relative to this language.
\paragraph{Variable exponent, pure Diophantine elimination requested.}
Exponentiation has a computable graph, so an MRDP representation can
replace the power predicates at the level of existence. This argument by
itself neither supplies the same small quartic nor preserves the unique
witness property. Those are separate tasks requiring control of the
replacement's fibers.
In particular the present construction does not establish a single-fold
or finite-fold version of MRDP. The infinite-loop quartic of the preceding
section escapes this issue because its two exponents are fixed by the
supplied finite grammar, not variable powers needing uniform elimination.

\section{Other FIFO computational substrates\srctag{20}}
\label{cdc:cq:sec:substrates}

\subsection{Deletion-tag systems}
\srcnote{\wtag{} [Part~VI compiles uncompressed deletion-tag runs with one coordinate per consumed symbol (\cref{cdc:qc:sec:general-tag}); the table below makes the same systems instances of the grammar compiler.]}


A deletion-$\delta$ tag system, with fixed $\delta\ge1$, associates an
appendant $A_a$ to each symbol $a\in\Sigma$. When the queue begins with
$a_1\cdots a_\delta$, it deletes those $\delta$ symbols and appends
$A_{a_1}$. It stops if fewer than $\delta$ symbols remain. Use the finite
action table
\[
 (a_1\cdots a_\delta\text{ read},\ A_{a_1}\text{ written})
 \qquad (a_1,\ldots,a_\delta\in\Sigma).
\]
The compiler then applies without any change. For fixed $\Sigma$ and
$\delta$, this is a fixed table; when these are variable problem inputs,
the table's size $|\Sigma|^\delta$ must not be hidden in a complexity
bound. The published universality and simulation results for 2-tag
systems\cite{woods-neary} are independent of the certificate proof.

An exact halting certificate for a supplied tag trace has a final word
$r$ with $|r|<\delta$. There is no legal post-halting padding because every
nonidentity tag action reads exactly $\delta$ symbols. The root resource
condition rejects any proposed action after a premature stop.

\subsection{Several reliable channels}

Suppose there are $d$ FIFO queues. An atomic action reads a fixed word
$u_{e,j}$ from each queue $j$ and then appends a fixed word $v_{e,j}$ to
that queue. All reads take place before all writes. A single finite
controller governs the action; the schedule is prescribed by the trace
grammar. Some reads and writes may be empty.

\begin{theorem}[Product extension to FIFO networks]
\label{cdc:cq:thm:multiqueue}
For a supplied control-compatible grammar and actual initial and final
words $q_j,r_j$ on $d$ queues, the exact execution relation has a
unique-witness quartic with
\begin{equation}
 N=d(6g+3c+1),\qquad M=d(6l+9c+3).
 \label{cdc:cq:eq:multicounts}
\end{equation}
It keeps no intermediate channel contents.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
For each channel $j$, form its total read and write words and its resource
pair using the same action order. Necessity follows by projecting an
execution to each channel. Conversely, the single-queue endpoint theorem
reconstructs each channel at each proposed action and proves that its read
is enabled. Therefore all reads of that action are simultaneously enabled;
the specified control path and the atomic write operations give a network
step. Induction reconstructs the whole network execution.

Allocate independent copies of the one-channel variables and residuals,
with a single common statically checked grammar. Their natural solutions
are independently unique. Adding their sums of squares yields a quartic
whose zero exists exactly when every channel condition holds, giving the
counts.
\end{proof}

\wtag{} Part~VI's fixed-read network certificate (\cref{cdc:qc:thm:network-certificate}) certifies uncompressed runs, with one coordinate per consumed symbol and read counts fixed by the phase; here a supplied global schedule is a grammar and the read words may depend on the action. This bears on \cref{cdc:q:readcounts}; see the note there.


The result concerns a \emph{specified global schedule}. It does not solve
schedule synthesis, arbitrary reachability in communicating machines,
fairness, or equivalence of schedules. Those are different problems.
For a specified repeated macro, the maximum number of common network
copies is the minimum of the per-channel maxima, treating a read-free
channel's bound as $\infty$. Infinite repeatability holds exactly when it
holds on all channels, so the corresponding loop quartics can likewise
be combined.

\subsection{Finite-state queue programs and machine simulations}

General finite-state queue programs are already covered by the action
definition. Known universality of queue automata\cite{kocher} makes this
class a Turing-complete substrate, while cyclic and deletion-tag programs
give particularly restricted instances. A simulation from another model
can therefore inherit these arithmetic representations after translation
into queue actions.

There is an important quantitative caveat. A simulation that preserves
computability need not preserve compressed trace size. To claim an
$O(g)$ certificate in the \emph{source} model's grammar size, one must also
prove a bound for translating source trace grammars into queue trace
grammars. The present article proves $O(g)$ bounds natively for the
supplied FIFO grammar, not automatically for every Turing-equivalent
formalism.

\section{Algorithmic consequences and impossibility boundaries\srctag{20}}
\label{cdc:cq:sec:limits}

\subsection{Arithmetic size versus binary witness size}

For a cyclic-tag trace of $T$ steps, $|U|=T$, and the root variable $P^U$
is $B^T$. Therefore this particular encoding necessarily has a witness
coordinate with
\[
 \lfloor T\log_2B\rfloor+1
\]
binary digits. The exponential-compression example is a direct witness to
this phenomenon. The theorem reduces the number of variables and equations;
it does not turn a numerically written assignment into a short bit string.

This is an encoding-specific observation, not a lower bound against every
possible Diophantine representation of the same relation. In particular
one must not conclude that polynomial-size numeric certificates are
impossible merely because our convenient radix scales are large.

\subsection{Polynomial-time verification of supplied compressed traces}

There is a separate compressed-word verification route. We use as an
external algorithmic input the established deterministic polynomial-time
algorithms for comparing straight-line-program words, obtainable in the
fully compressed word setting studied by Je\.{z}\cite{jez}. Prefix
extraction and binary powering add only polynomially many grammar nodes.

\begin{corollary}[Deciding a supplied grammar without large radix integers]
\label{cdc:cq:cor:compresseddecision}
For a fixed finite action table, the following can be decided in time
polynomial in the sizes of the supplied trace and word grammars:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=9mm]
\item whether the supplied finite trace connects the supplied endpoints;
\item whether a supplied closed macro repeats indefinitely from the
supplied initial word;
\item the exact value $N_{\max}$, written in binary, or the answer
$\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Word lengths are computed by addition over the grammars and have polynomial
binary length. Resource pairs use addition, subtraction, and comparison
of integers with those lengths. Total read and write word grammars are
obtained from the trace grammar by replacing each action leaf with its
read or write word.

For (a), use the endpoint theorem, compute the resource guard, and compare
the two compressed words $qV$ and $Ur$. For (b), handle $a=0$ and $b<a$
separately. In the remaining case compute $d=\gcd(a,b)$, build the two
powers in \eqref{cdc:cq:eq:conjugacy} by binary concatenation, and compare the
resulting compressed words.

For (c), first compare the initial prefix and then the two periodic tails
only up to total length $L+a+b-d$ when $b>0$, or up to $L$ when $b=0$.
The periodic prefixes are represented by binary powers of $U$ and $V$,
truncated to the required length. Binary search on the prefix length,
using compressed word equality at each comparison, finds the first
mismatch. The number of comparisons is logarithmic in the represented
length and hence polynomial in grammar size. No mismatch by the stated
threshold implies an infinite common prefix by Fine--Wilf. Finally apply
\eqref{cdc:cq:eq:maxrepeat}. The finite answer has polynomial binary length since
it is bounded by a quotient of the tested prefix lengths or by the
length-resource bound.
\end{proof}

This corollary relies on a standard compressed-word algorithm, not on a
new fast integer-polynomial root finder. The included Python implementation
uses exact natural integers for the arithmetic compiler and explicit words
for the loop analyzer; it does not implement a state-of-the-art compressed
word equality algorithm. Its measured runtimes should not be mistaken for
a realization of every asymptotic claim in this corollary.

\wtag{} The corollary rests on an external algorithm \cite{jez} that the package does not implement; the caveat just stated is the manuscript's own.


\subsection{No computable universal bound on accepting trace grammars}

We isolate an intrinsic limit on automatic compression. Let $\mathcal U$
be a fixed deterministic universal queue program with a computably
undecidable accepted-halting set on a decidable class of input encodings.
Normalize acceptance to a distinguished final state with an empty queue.
This can be achieved by appending a fresh end marker on acceptance and
then deleting symbols until that marker is reached. Rejecting stops may
be replaced by infinite loops, so accepted halting and divergence can be
taken to be the only two outcomes on valid inputs.

These harmless finite-control conventions are used only for the following
computability arguments. They do not assert that a particular minimal
cyclic-tag program has already been implemented in the package.

\srcnote{\wtag{} [The finite search of \cref{cdc:bd:prop:nobound}, and of manuscript~06's bound on scheme parameters (\cref{cdc:cs:prop:nobound}), applied to grammar size.]}
\begin{theorem}[No total computable grammar-size bound]
\label{cdc:cq:thm:nobound}
There is no total computable function $f:\N\to\N$ such that every
accepted-halting input word $q$ of length $n$ for $\mathcal U$ has an
accepting trace grammar with at most $f(n)$ nodes.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Suppose such an $f$ exists. On input $q$, compute $f(|q|)$ and enumerate
all topologically ordered trace grammars of at most that size over the
fixed finite transition alphabet. There are finitely many: every node is
a leaf with one of finitely many action labels or a pair of earlier node
indices. Reject grammars with incompatible control endpoints or the wrong
initial or accepting state.

For each remaining grammar, decide whether its root trace carries $q$ to
the empty queue. The endpoint theorem supplies a terminating decision
procedure, even without using the polynomial-time version of
Corollary~\ref{cdc:cq:cor:compresseddecision}. Accept if one grammar works and
reject if all fail. The assumed bound makes this a decision procedure for
the accepted-halting set, contradicting its undecidability.
\end{proof}

The quantifiers matter. The theorem says that every proposed total
computable bound fails on some accepted-halting input. It does not say
that minimum grammar size is eventually larger than every computable
function on every input length, or that every long trace is
incompressible. It is a nonexistence theorem for a uniform bound, not a
pointwise asymptotic estimate.

\subsection{Periodic transition lassos cannot characterize all divergence}

\srcnote{\wtag{} [For priority arithmetic Part~XII proves more: eventual periodicity is computably enumerable-complete even for one fixed program (\cref{cdc:pf:thm:ep}). The neighbouring report \emph{liveness-beyond-halting} makes the corresponding remark for counter lassos, after its Proposition \texttt{lbh:qd:prop:lasso}.]}
\begin{theorem}[Incompleteness of periodic-transition certificates]
\label{cdc:cq:thm:nolassocomplete}
A deterministic universal queue program with undecidable halting and only
halting or divergence on its valid inputs has divergent runs whose
transition traces are not ultimately periodic.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Assume every divergent run has an ultimately periodic transition trace.
Enumerate a finite transition prefix and a nonempty closed transition
macro. Simulate the prefix; if it is executable, obtain its actual entry
queue word. Decide whether the macro is indefinitely repeatable there,
using Theorem~\ref{cdc:cq:thm:conjugacy}, with the read-free case handled
separately. A successful pair is a sound certificate of divergence.
Under the assumption, every divergent input eventually has a successful
pair in this enumeration.

Thus divergence would be computably enumerable. Halting is also
computably enumerable by simulation. Dovetailing these two procedures
would decide halting, a contradiction.
\end{proof}

The theorem rules out completeness even when the periodic tail is allowed
to grow the queue without bound. It is therefore stronger than merely
observing that some divergent runs never repeat a complete configuration.
The compact infinite-loop quartics prove real infinite behavior, but only
for a properly restricted family of behaviors.

\subsection{Why this does not settle single-fold MRDP}

For fixed $G,q,r$, the finite polynomial has at most one witness. However,
a single halting computation generally has many descriptions: unused
grammar nodes, different binary bracketing, repeated subexpressions, and
different decompositions can all describe the same trace. Even a canonical
choice of grammar, if effectively specified, would not by itself give a
fixed-arity single-fold Diophantine representation of universal halting.
It would still be necessary to represent an unbounded grammar and its
verification uniformly with controlled fibers.

The difference is visible in the syntax:
\[
 \text{a family }Q_G(\mathbf x_G)=0
 \qquad\text{versus}\qquad
 P(e,q,\mathbf y)=0
\]
with one fixed finite tuple $\mathbf y$. Our tuple $\mathbf x_G$ grows
with the supplied grammar. MRDP can turn a computably enumerable coding
of the whole construction into an existence statement for a fixed
polynomial, but an existence-preserving translation is not automatically
witness-preserving. The same warning applies to eliminating the power
predicates of Section~\ref{cdc:cq:sec:powered}.

\wtag{} The same gap is Part~IX's finite-fold boundary (manuscript~07's form in \cref{cdc:qc:sec:finite-fold}; \cref{cdc:bd:thm:universal}) and \cref{cdc:q:compression}.


\section{Implementation and reproducible validation\srctag{20}}
\label{cdc:cq:sec:validation}

The accompanying implementation uses Python's standard library and exact
integers. No numerical tolerance, floating-point logarithm, randomized
identity test, or external computer algebra system is used to decide the
recorded assertions. Random test generation has the fixed seed
$20261002$; every tested property is then checked exactly.

\subsection{Executable components}

\path{code/20-compressed-queue-queue_certificates.py} supplies action and grammar data
structures, radix encoding, resource composition, the finite compiler,
a sparse integer-polynomial type, the ordinary infinite-loop compiler,
word and resource power identities, a small-trace simulator, and the exact
macro repetition analyzer. The sparse representation maps a sorted tuple
of variable indices to an integer coefficient. It can export either the
quadratic residual list or the collected sum-of-squares polynomial.

The finite compiler constructs the uniquely forced node data. On a failed
resource guard it assigns zero to the candidate slack and then correctly
rejects that candidate; it does not return a negative purported natural
witness. Invalid syntax or control composition raises a descriptive error.
The theoretical constant-$1$ convention for malformed grammars is
therefore implemented as an early structural rejection.

\path{code/20-compressed-queue-verify.py} runs the checks and rewrites
\path{data/20-compressed-queue-verification.json}. It also regenerates both small exported
polynomial examples. The powered-schema \emph{identities} are tested,
including empty words, but the JSON exporter emits ordinary quartics for
straight-line finite traces and fixed infinite loops; it does not export
variable-exponent formulas.

\subsection{Recorded check families}

The recorded run used Python 3.13.5 and completed $259{,}025$ assertions.
The following table identifies major families without suggesting that
finite testing proves a theorem.
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{p{0.70\textwidth}r}
\toprule
Check family & Assertions\\
\midrule
Exhaustive binary endpoint equivalence for traces of lengths 1--3 & 144,746\\
Resource drift and direct prefix-deficit formula & 41,356\\
Finite resource associativity and unique minimum gadget & 4,177\\
Random multisymbol/empty-word endpoint checks & 5,000\\
Power resource and read/write encoding identities & 15,000\\
Fine--Wilf checks over all binary periods of lengths 1--5 and shifts & 15,996\\
Finite compiler versus direct simulation & 700\\
Ordinary infinite-loop compiler versus exact loop criterion & 800\\
Exact infinite-loop conjugacy comparisons & 6,000\\
One-coordinate mutations rejected in valid finite witnesses & 5,100\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Additional assertions check exact dimension formulas, polynomial degrees,
collected polynomial evaluation, finite pumping, first failed macro
counts, control rejection, the causality counterexample, and the large
repeated trace. The JSON receipt gives every category and its count.

The endpoint enumeration uses all $14$ actions formed by a one-bit read
and a binary write word of length at most two, all $2{,}954$ nonempty
traces of lengths one through three, and all seven binary words of length
at most two at each endpoint. Thus $2{,}954\cdot7\cdot7=144{,}746$ is a
fully specified finite domain, not an unspecified search sample.

For the random loop tests, $6{,}000$ cases were examined, of which $83$
were classified as indefinitely repeatable. Their finite simulations are
cross-checks, not the basis of the infinite assertion; the mathematical
basis is the conjugacy theorem. In $800$ further cases, the actual
ordinary quartic's natural candidate witness was checked against that
criterion. For accepted examples, changing individual witness
coordinates was also checked to destroy the zero.

\subsection{Reproduction and trust boundaries}

From the package directory run
\srcnote{\wtag{} [The delivered layout, in which \path{code/verify.py} imports \path{queue_certificates} by name and writes \path{data/}: run it in a copy in which the shipped files carry their delivered names (this report's README). The manuscript's \path{article.tex} is not shipped.]}
\begin{lstlisting}
python code/verify.py
latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error article.tex
\end{lstlisting}
The polynomial examples are data, not trusted executable proofs.
The separate script \path{code/20-compressed-queue-check_certificate.py} checks their
integer syntax, natural witness values, degree bounds, and the exact
identity of the exported polynomial with the sum of residual squares.
It does not import the compiler.
A simple checker can independently evaluate every exported monomial on
the listed witness and verify the residual degrees. Such checking proves
that \emph{that assignment} is a zero. The statements that all zeros
correspond to executions, that every execution has a zero, and that the
zero is unique rely on the mathematical compiler proof, not merely on
successful numerical evaluation.

No universal-machine experiment, Lean kernel check, exhaustive
bibliographic novelty certification, or proof of the full correctness of
the Python interpreter is included. These limitations are explicit so
that the reproducibility receipt has its proper meaning.

\paragraph{\wtag{} The research tree's review.} Batch~79, 2 October 2026. ProveIt's Hilbert's-tenth-problem research tree, maintained separately, reviewed this archive \cite{repo-cqrev}. It finds no theorem-level defect in the endpoint, resource, repetition, Fine--Wilf and conjugacy, infinite-loop or powered-grammar arguments, and reproduces two defects of the low-level constructors. First, \code{Poly(terms)} at line~132 of \path{code/20-compressed-queue-queue_certificates.py} accepts noninteger coefficients: for \code{Poly({(): float(2**60), (0,): -1.0})} the natural witness $2^{60}+1$ gives the floating residual $0.0$, and a directly constructed \code{Certificate} accepts, although the exact residual is $-1$. Second, \code{Action(read=['0'], write='0')} is accepted and keeps the caller's mutable list, so changing the list after compilation leaves the old certificate at zero while a fresh compilation rejects. The compiler's own output is unaffected (it emits integer coefficients, and \path{code/20-compressed-queue-check_certificate.py} rejects floating coefficients), and no theorem is touched. The tested repair \path{compressed_queue_exact_inputs.patch} in \path{Computability/HilbertTenthProblem/Papers/research-wip/native-stream-queue/} requires exact strings, integers and sorted natural monomials; it is not applied here, because the shipped program is the delivered bytes. On the original and the repaired copies all 259,025 author checks pass and both exports are byte-identical to the delivered ones; the review's own helper adds 1,425 assertions.


\section{Formalization targets and further research\srctag{20}}
\label{cdc:cq:sec:research}

\subsection{A focused path into ProveIt}

The predecessor's integration note already recommends separating word
semantics, resource legality, polynomial evaluation, and witness
uniqueness\cite{repo-qcint}. The compressed development can follow the
same architecture with a new grammar layer.

First define the partial length maps and prove
Lemma~\ref{cdc:cq:lem:resourcecomposition}. This gives associativity and the
power formula without manipulating long prefix lists. Next prove the
word-level endpoint theorem independently of radix encoding. The crucial
induction step uses $|q|\ge|u|$ before cancelling the first read word;
formalizing that order prevents exactly the ghost-read error.

Define a finite acyclic grammar with explicit backward references, and
interpret it both as a trace and as a tuple of word/resource summaries.
A structural induction proves equality of these interpretations. Reify
the residuals as integer multivariate polynomials and prove their
soundness and unique reconstructibility over $\N$. Degree and variable
counts should be separate lemmas, so that simplifying the generated
polynomial cannot silently change what is counted.

For infinite loops, formalize finite-word conjugacy first. The implication
$Aq=qB\Rightarrow A^nq=qB^n$ is elementary and supports a finite-prefix
formulation of infinite-word equality. Infinite behavior can then be
expressed as the executability of every finite power; deterministic
compatibility reconstructs the run. Fine--Wilf is needed for the numerical
pumping bound, but \emph{not} for the conjugacy-based quartic theorem.
This dependency separation makes the central nontermination certificate
available before a full periodicity library is finished.

\subsection{Research questions with explicit targets}
\srcnote{\wtag{} [Manuscript~20 posed its ten items as numbered paragraphs; they are question environments here, titled by their headings, with unchanged text. A \wtag{} line after six of them names a related result or question of this report; the items are not merged.]}


\begin{question}[Better constants without losing transparent uniqueness; source 20]\label{cdc:cq:q:constants}
The finite compiler uses nine coordinates per concatenation in the worst
case, counting its six summary outputs and three minimum witnesses.
Can one eliminate resource auxiliaries or share word/resource coordinates
while retaining a sparse quartic and a direct unique-witness proof?
A useful comparison must state whether leaves, supplied endpoint codes,
and unused grammar nodes are counted. The target is an improved uniform
constant, not a claim that the present count is optimal.
\end{question}

\wtag{} Batch~79, 2 October 2026: answered in part by the research tree's projection after \cref{cdc:cq:thm:compiler}, which eliminates the leaf and the resource auxiliaries and keeps a sparse quartic with unique witnesses: $6c+1$ coordinates and $6c+3$ residuals \cite{repo-cqrev}. Optimality is not addressed.

\begin{question}[A cubic boundary for compressed FIFO certificates; source 20]\label{cdc:cq:q:cubic}
The sum-of-squares mechanism gives degree four because word concatenation
and cancellation produce quadratic residuals. Is there a comparably
explicit, unique-witness cubic construction in a suitable restricted
nonnegative form? Any candidate should be tested first on a single word
concatenation gate and on the exact minimum relation. Lower bounds would
need a precisely defined class of encodings; degree alone is too vague.
\end{question}

\wtag{} Compare Part~XI's classification of polynomials of degree at most three that are nonnegative on the real orthant (\cref{cdc:of:thm:classification}) and Part~XVI's cubic certificates.

\begin{question}[Canonical semantic summaries on compressed words; source 20]\label{cdc:cq:q:summaries}
Formula~\eqref{cdc:cq:eq:saturated} separates the raw resource threshold from
its content-sensitive saturation. Can a shortest semantic queue-action
normal form be computed and arithmetized directly from a trace SLP,
with witnesses still linear in its grammar size? This should be compared
explicitly with existing queue-monoid normal forms\cite{hkz}, rather than
presented as a rediscovery of them.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Multiple parametric phases; source 20]\label{cdc:cq:q:phases}
For a single fixed macro, feasible repetition counts form an initial
segment and admit \eqref{cdc:cq:eq:maxrepeat}. What useful classes of schemas
$\tau_1^{k_1}\cdots\tau_m^{k_m}$ admit pure polynomial, fiber-controlled
certificates without a general exponentiation predicate? Commuting
output periods, synchronized channels, or a fixed primitive read period
are natural first restrictions. A complete statement must include the
intermediate content alignment, not merely resource inequalities.
\end{question}

\wtag{} Compare Part~III's nested repetition schedules (\cref{cdc:cs:thm:compiler}), Part~XII's flat schedules (\cref{cdc:pf:cor:flat}) and \cref{cdc:q:storage}.

\begin{question}[Beyond periodic nontermination; source 20]\label{cdc:cq:q:periodic}
The incompleteness theorem forces richer witnesses if one wants to cover
more divergent universal runs. Morphic, substitution-generated, or
recursively nested transition descriptions may be useful next classes.
The objective is a sound decidably checkable subclass with a clear
semantic theorem; completeness for all divergence is excluded by
computability. It would be valuable to exhibit concrete universal-queue
runs separating several such certificate classes.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Compression across simulation boundaries; source 20]\label{cdc:cq:q:simulation}
A queue simulation of a tag system, rewriting system, or other universal
model preserves existence of computation but may destroy source-level
sharing. Establish grammar-preserving simulation theorems with explicit
size and control-state overhead. Such theorems would extend the native
FIFO bounds to genuinely different substrates, rather than merely
invoke Turing equivalence.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Partial-order compression for FIFO networks; source 20]\label{cdc:cq:q:partialorder}
Our network grammar supplies a total action order. When actions commute
on disjoint queues, can one quotient schedules by trace equivalence and
still obtain one arithmetic witness per \emph{semantic trace class}?
Resource commutation is not enough when several actions touch the same
channel: FIFO content order and causal availability must be preserved.
This is a promising meeting point with the repository's existing causal
trace work, but requires a distinct proof of canonicalization.
\end{question}

\wtag{} The repository's causal trace work is Parts~I--II (\cref{cdc:part:traces}).

\begin{question}[Loss, priorities, and admissible nondeterminism; source 20]\label{cdc:cq:q:loss}
Reliable queues are the cleanest setting for endpoint reconstruction.
For lossy or priority channels, deleting symbols or overtaking messages
changes the word equation into an embedding or reordered relation.
Identify exactly which semantics admit a comparable compressed,
uniquely witnessed certificate, and which create unavoidable witness
multiplicity. The acceleration literature already distinguishes these
models sharply\cite{kocher}.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Proof-producing trace compression in practice; source 20]\label{cdc:cq:q:practice}
Theorem~\ref{cdc:cq:thm:nobound} forbids a complete computable bound, not useful
heuristics. A practical compressor could infer repeated blocks, build a
DAG, and emit the quartic plus a symbolic trace proof. Benchmarks should
report expanded length, grammar nodes, polynomial monomials, maximum
coordinate bit length, and compressed verification cost separately.
Comparing only the number of variables would hide the principal numeric
cost of the radix encoding.
\end{question}

\wtag{} Compare \cref{cdc:q:acceleration}.

\begin{question}[Certified exports and fiber-sensitive reflection; source 20]\label{cdc:cq:q:exports}
A Lean checker for the exported sparse polynomial could verify syntax,
backward references, degree, and exact reification. The higher-value goal
is proving that the exported construction preserves the empty/singleton
fiber theorem. For the powered-schema extension, any proposed removal
of the power predicates should be accompanied by an explicit theorem on
its auxiliary fibers, not just its projection onto the original variables.
\end{question}

\wtag{} Compare \cref{cdc:q:verified}.

\section{Conclusion\srctag{20}}\label{cdc:cq:sec:conclusion}

The arithmetic representation of a queue execution need not mirror its
entire history. Total read and write words handle content; an exact
resource pair handles causality; and grammar composition handles sharing.
Together these give a single quartic with $6g+3c+1$ natural variables and
exactly one zero for every valid supplied execution.

The same separation also makes a useful part of infinite computation
finite. A repeated macro fails either through resource exhaustion or
through a first mismatch of two eventually periodic streams. Its exact
number of successful copies follows from those two obstructions.
Infinite repeatability becomes the finite equation
$U^{b/d}q=qV^{a/d}$, and binary word-power circuits turn that equation into
an ordinary unique-witness quartic of grammar-linear size.

These are stronger outputs than the bare assertion that halting is
Diophantine: they specify the equations, count their variables, reconstruct
their witnesses, and include sound finite certificates for a nontrivial
class of divergent runs. Their limitations are equally structural.
Numeric witnesses may remain enormous, trace grammars must be supplied,
periodic lassos do not cover all universal divergence, and variable-power
elimination does not automatically preserve single-foldness. Keeping
those boundaries explicit makes the constructions suitable foundations
for further formal and computational work.
